title: Maths Revision Set
subject: Maths
desc: Ten pages covering counting to 20, number bonds to 10 and 20, adding and taking away within 20, simple word problems and the 2 times table.
obj: Count, order and compare numbers to 20
Add and subtract within 20, including word problems
Count in twos and recall the 2 times table

guide.what: Your child counts objects to 20, reads and writes the numbers, and learns that 11 to 19 are one ten and some ones.
steps: Count real things, touching each one as you say the number.
Write 1 to 20 on a strip of paper. Point as you count forwards, then backwards.
Show 14 as a bundle of 10 sticks and 4 loose sticks: one ten and four ones.
home: Count rotis, stairs or cars on the road.
Ask: What comes after 13? What comes before 20?
guide.watch: Teen numbers are often written backwards, like 41 for 14. Say "ten comes first" and write the 1 first.

title: Numbers to 20 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 4 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on numbers to 20, from "Count and Write" to "Tens and Ones". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Count objects up to 20 and write the matching numeral.
Order numbers to 20 forwards, backwards and in twos.
Find the number before, after and between numbers to 20; compare two numbers.
Understand teen numbers as one ten and some ones; order numbers to 20.

guide.what: Your child counts objects to 20, reads and writes the numbers, and learns that 11 to 19 are one ten and some ones.
steps: Count real things, touching each one as you say the number.
Write 1 to 20 on a strip of paper. Point as you count forwards, then backwards.
Show 14 as a bundle of 10 sticks and 4 loose sticks: one ten and four ones.
home: Count rotis, stairs or cars on the road.
Ask: What comes after 13? What comes before 20?
guide.watch: Teen numbers are often written backwards, like 41 for 14. Say "ten comes first" and write the 1 first.

title: Number Bonds Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 4 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on number bonds, from "Number Bonds to 10" to "How Many More to Make 10?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use number bonds to make 20 and other numbers up to 20.
Recall number bonds for numbers up to 9.
Use bonds to 10 to find how many more are needed.

guide.what: Two smaller numbers join to make a bigger number, like 6 and 4 make 10.
steps: Put 10 chickpeas in a line and slide some to one side: 7 here, 3 there.
Draw the bond: a big circle for the whole, two small circles for the parts.
Ask it both ways: "7 and what make 10?" and "10 is 7 and what?"
home: Show 10 fingers and fold some down. How many are still up?
Play "make 10" with playing cards.
guide.watch: Counting every dot is fine at first. Praise your child when they start to remember a bond without counting.

title: Addition Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 4 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on addition, from "Adding Within 10" to "Adding Three Numbers". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Add two numbers with a total up to 10.
Add within 20 and solve simple word problems.
Add three small numbers with a total up to 20.

guide.what: Adding means putting groups together to find how many there are in all.
steps: Make two groups of objects, push them together and count them all.
Move on to counting on: start at the bigger number and count up the smaller one.
Use a number line: start at the first number and hop forward.
home: Add the prices of two sweets at the shop.
Roll two dice and add the dots.
guide.watch: When hopping on a number line, children often count the number they start on. From 8 to 9 is one hop.

title: Subtraction Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 4 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on subtraction, from "Taking Away Within 10" to "Counting Back". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Subtract within 10 by taking away objects.
Subtract within 20 and solve take away word problems.
Find missing numbers in subtraction sentences.
Subtract within 20 by counting back on a number line.

guide.what: Taking away means removing some and finding how many are left.
steps: Act it out: 8 biscuits, eat 3, count what is left.
Cross out pictures to show the ones taken away.
Count back on a number line from the bigger number.
home: Make story sums at meals: 10 grapes, you ate 4. How many are left?
Hide some buttons under a cup. How many are hidden?
guide.watch: Children sometimes write the smaller number first, like 3 − 8. Always start with how many you had.

title: The 2 Times Table Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on 2 times table, from "The 2 Times Table" to "Twos Word Problems". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Count in twos and recall the 2 times table to 10 × 2.
Count in steps of two to 20.
Solve simple word problems using the 2 times table.

guide.what: Counting in twos, and knowing that 3 × 2 means three groups of two.
steps: Pair up shoes or socks and count them in twos.
Say the twos chant together: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
Link it to doubles: 4 × 2 is the same as 4 + 4.
home: Count the pairs of shoes at the door.
Clap on every second number while counting to 20.
guide.watch: Saying the chant is not the same as understanding it. Ask: How many groups? How many in each group?

title: Science Revision Set
subject: Science
desc: Ten pages on energy, heat, light and sound, with sorting, true or false and fill in the blank activities taken from everyday life at home and school.
obj: Know that energy makes things move, grow and work
Sort hot and cold things and name sources of heat
Sort natural and man-made light; explain shadows
Sort loud and soft sounds and know we hear with our ears

guide.what: Energy makes things move, grow and work. People get energy from food; machines get it from electricity.
steps: Ask: What makes the fan move? What lets you run and play?
Sort things that need electricity from things that do not.
Talk about food as fuel for the body.
home: Spot everything that uses electricity in one room.
Go on a switch-off patrol for lights nobody is using.
guide.watch: Keep it concrete. Your child does not need a deep explanation of electricity yet.

title: Energy Practice
subject: Science
desc: 4 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on energy, from "We Need Energy" to "Saving Energy". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Understand that energy is needed to move, grow and work.
Know that food gives us energy and some foods are healthier than others.
Sort everyday objects by whether they use electricity.
Know simple ways to save energy at home.

guide.what: Energy makes things move, grow and work. People get energy from food; machines get it from electricity.
steps: Ask: What makes the fan move? What lets you run and play?
Sort things that need electricity from things that do not.
Talk about food as fuel for the body.
home: Spot everything that uses electricity in one room.
Go on a switch-off patrol for lights nobody is using.
guide.watch: Keep it concrete. Your child does not need a deep explanation of electricity yet.

title: Heat Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on heat, from "Hot or Cold?" to "Heat Changes Things". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort everyday things as hot or cold.
Name sources of heat and stay safe around them.
Describe simple changes caused by heating.

guide.what: Some things are hot and some are cold, and heat can change things, like melting ice.
steps: Feel warm and cold water and describe each one.
Name sources of heat: the sun, a stove, a heater, a fire.
Watch heat change something: ice melting, a roti cooking.
home: Put an ice cube in the sun and check it after 10 minutes.
Talk about winter clothes and summer clothes.
guide.watch: Always pair heat with safety: look, do not touch.

title: Light Practice
subject: Science
desc: 4 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on light, from "Sources of Light" to "Shiny or Dull?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort sources of light into natural and made by people.
Know that we need light to see and that blocked light makes a shadow.
Tell the difference between day and night.
Sort materials as shiny or dull.

guide.what: We need light to see. Light comes from the sun or from things people make. Blocking light makes a shadow.
steps: Switch the lights off and on. Can we see in the dark?
Sort natural light and light made by people.
Use a torch to make a shadow bigger and smaller.
home: Make shadow puppets on the wall.
Find shiny and dull things in the kitchen.
guide.watch: Many children think the moon makes its own light. Explain that the sun lights it up.

title: Sound Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on sound, from "Loud or Soft?" to "Science Review". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort sounds as loud or soft.
Match animals to their sounds and know we hear with our ears.
Review energy, heat, light and sound.

guide.what: Sounds are made when things shake. We hear with our ears, and sounds can be loud or soft.
steps: Hum with a hand on your throat to feel it shake.
Make loud and soft sounds with a spoon and a pot.
Match animals to the sounds they make.
home: Play a one-minute listening game.
Make a shaker from a bottle and some daal.
guide.watch: Remind your child that very loud sounds can hurt our ears.

title: Social Studies Revision Set
subject: Social Studies
desc: Ten pages on family, feelings and house rules. Children write and draw about their own family, name feelings and choose safe, kind actions at home.
obj: Talk, draw and write about my own family
Name family members in English and Urdu
Name feelings and choose calm, kind actions
Follow house rules and stay safe at home

guide.what: Who is in my family, family words in English and Urdu, and how we help at home.
steps: Look at family photos and name each person.
Say English and Urdu words together: grandmother, Dadi or Nani.
Talk about the jobs each person does at home.
home: Draw a family tree together.
Give one small helping job each day.
guide.watch: Families look different. Make sure every kind of family feels normal to your child.

title: My Family Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 4 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on family, from "My Family" to "Helping at Home". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Talk and write about members of my own family.
Name family members in English and Urdu.
Compare family sizes and know what a joint family is.
Identify ways children can help their family.

guide.what: Who is in my family, family words in English and Urdu, and how we help at home.
steps: Look at family photos and name each person.
Say English and Urdu words together: grandmother, Dadi or Nani.
Talk about the jobs each person does at home.
home: Draw a family tree together.
Give one small helping job each day.
guide.watch: Families look different. Make sure every kind of family feels normal to your child.

title: Feelings Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on feelings, from "How Do They Feel?" to "What Can I Do?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name feelings and link them to everyday situations.
Express my own feelings in pictures and words.
Choose calm and kind ways to deal with feelings.

guide.what: Naming feelings and choosing calm, kind ways to deal with them.
steps: Name your own feelings out loud: "I feel tired."
Draw or act out happy, sad, angry and scared faces.
Practise one calm-down step, like three slow breaths.
home: At bedtime, ask about the best and hardest part of the day.
While reading a story, ask how a character feels.
guide.watch: Do not tell a child not to feel something. Accept the feeling, then guide what they do.

title: House Rules Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on house rules, from "House Rules" to "Social Studies Review". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Recognise safe and unsafe actions at home and know emergency numbers.
Review family, feelings and house rules.

guide.what: Why homes have rules, good manners, and how to stay safe.
steps: Make three simple house rules together.
Explain the reason behind each rule.
Practise what to do in an emergency, including the numbers 15 and 1122.
home: Put a rules chart on the fridge.
Role-play the doorbell: always ask a grown-up first.
guide.watch: Keep rules few and clear. Too many rules are hard to remember.

title: Pencil control Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Nursery English practice on pencil control, from "Lines Left to Right" to "Loops and Circles". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Hold a pencil and trace straight and slanting lines.
Trace curved and zigzag lines from left to right.
Trace loops and circles with control.

guide.what: Strong, steady pencil movements that later become letters.
steps: Show how to hold the pencil in a pinch grip near the tip.
Trace the line in the air with a finger first, then on paper.
Go slowly from the green dot to the star without lifting the pencil.
home: Draw lines in a tray of flour or sand.
Pick up chickpeas one at a time to build finger strength.
guide.watch: A fist grip is common at this age. Gently move the fingers into a pinch and keep sessions short.

title: Letter sounds a to m Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Nursery English practice on letter sounds a to m, from "Trace a b c d" to "Trace j k l m". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Trace the letters a to d and say their sounds.
Trace the letters e to i and say their sounds.
Trace j to m and hear first sounds in words.

pages.title: Trace e f g h i

guide.what: Children hear and say the sound of each letter and trace its shape.
steps: Say the sound, not the letter name: "a" as in apple.
Show a real object that starts with that sound.
Trace the letter while saying the sound.
home: Make a sound basket: collect things that start with the same sound.
Sing a letter sounds song while pointing to letters.
guide.watch: b and d look alike. Trace b as "bat then ball": the line first, then the circle.

title: Letter sounds n to z Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Nursery English practice on letter sounds n to z, from "Trace n o p q r" to "Trace x y z". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Trace the letters n to r and say their sounds.
Trace the letters s to w and say their sounds.
Trace x to z and hear first sounds in words.

pages.title: Trace n o p q r
Trace s t u v w

guide.what: The sounds and shapes of the letters n to z.
steps: Say the sound and a word: "s" as in sun.
Ask your child to find something at home with that sound.
Trace the letter, saying the sound each time.
home: Play I Spy with sounds.
Trace a letter on your child's back and let them guess it.
guide.watch: Some sounds are close, like s and z. Let your child feel the buzz of z on their throat.

title: Numbers 1 to 5 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on numbers 1 to 5, from "Count and Circle" to "Count and Write". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Count up to 5 objects and match the numeral.
Trace and say the numerals 1 to 5.
Count groups up to 5 and write the number.

guide.what: Counting up to 5 objects, saying one number for each, and knowing the numerals 1 to 5.
steps: Line up five objects and touch each one as you count.
Ask "how many?" and let your child say the last number.
Show the number card that matches the group.
home: Count spoons, shoes or biscuits at home.
Hold up fingers quickly and ask how many.
guide.watch: Children often count an object twice or skip one. Move each object aside as you count it.

title: Numbers 6 to 10 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on numbers 6 to 10, from "Count and Circle" to "Count and Write". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Count 6 to 10 objects and match the numeral.
Trace and say the numerals 6 to 10.
Count groups from 6 to 10 and write the number.

guide.what: Counting up to 10 objects and knowing the numerals 6 to 10.
steps: Count to 10 together on your fingers.
Make groups of 6 to 10 buttons and count them.
Match each group to a number card.
home: Count the steps as you climb the stairs.
Play hide and seek and count to 10 aloud.
guide.watch: Many children say "8, 9, 10" but skip 7. Count slowly together.

title: Shapes Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on shapes, from "Colour the Shapes" to "Trace the Shapes". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name circles, squares, triangles, stars and hearts.
Trace basic shapes with a steady hand.

guide.what: Naming circles, squares, triangles and other shapes, and finding them around us.
steps: Show a real object: a roti is a circle, a book is a rectangle.
Trace the shape in the air with a finger.
Count the sides and corners together.
home: Go on a shape hunt in the kitchen.
Make shapes with ice-cream sticks.
guide.watch: A triangle turned upside down is still a triangle. Turn shapes around and name them again.

title: My body Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on my body, from "My Five Senses" to "Keeping Clean". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the sense organs and what they do.
Count body parts and write the number.
Know simple habits that keep us clean and healthy.

guide.what: Naming body parts and our five senses, and keeping our body clean.
steps: Play "touch your nose, touch your ears".
Talk about what each sense does: eyes see, ears hear.
Make hand washing a song: count to 20 while washing.
home: Sing a body parts song with actions.
Play a smell or taste guessing game with safe foods.
guide.watch: Mixing up left and right is fine at this age. Just name the body part.

title: Colours Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on colours, from "Colour Them Right" to "Colour Sort". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name and use the main colours.
Match everyday things to their colours.

guide.what: Naming colours and matching them to things around us.
steps: Name the colour of things your child uses: red cup, blue shirt.
Sort toys or clothes into colour groups.
Mix two paints to see a new colour.
home: Colour hunt: find five green things at home.
Sort socks by colour.
guide.watch: Some children mix up blue and green for a long time. Keep naming both in daily talk.

title: Animals Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on animals, from "Animal Sounds" to "Farm or Jungle?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Match animals to the sounds they make.
Match animals to where they live.
Sort farm animals and wild animals.

guide.what: Naming animals, their sounds and homes, and sorting farm and wild animals.
steps: Show pictures or toys and make each animal sound.
Ask where each animal lives.
Sort animal toys into farm and jungle groups.
home: Visit a park or farm and name the animals you see.
Play guess the animal from its sound.
guide.watch: Use real names along with baby words: "cow", not only "moo-moo".

title: لکیروں کی مشق کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on line practice (لکیروں کی مشق), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Trace straight lines from right to left.
Trace curved and zigzag lines from right to left.
Trace loops and circles from right to left.

guide.what: Pencil movements from right to left, the direction Urdu is written.
steps: Show that Urdu starts on the right side of the page.
Trace each line in the air from right to left.
Trace on paper from the green dot to the star.
home: Draw right-to-left lines in a tray of flour.
Practise with a finger on a takhti or chalkboard.
guide.watch: Children used to English may start on the left. Put a green sticker on the right edge of the page.

title: حروف ا سے خ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on letters alif to khay (حروف ا سے خ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Trace and name ا ب پ ت.
Trace and name ٹ ث ج چ.
Trace ح خ and find ب among similar letters.

guide.what: Recognising and tracing the first ten Urdu letters, from alif to khay.
steps: Say the letter name and its sound: "bay" says "b".
Show how dots change a letter: ب has one dot below, ت has two above.
Trace the letter from right to left.
home: Make letters from playdough or roti dough.
Find ب and ت on food packets.
guide.watch: Dots are the tricky part. Count the dots together and say where they go: above or below.

title: حروف د سے ی کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on letters daal to yay (حروف د سے ی), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Trace and name د ذ ر ز.
Trace and name س ش ک گ.
Trace and name م ن و ی.

guide.what: Recognising and tracing more Urdu letters, from daal to yay.
steps: Say the letter name and a word that starts with it: س for سیب.
Compare look-alike letters: د and ذ, ر and ز.
Trace slowly from the right.
home: Play letter snap with homemade cards.
Point to letters in a story book and name them.
guide.watch: Look-alike pairs (ر ز، د ذ) get mixed up. The only difference is the dot, so point to it every time.

title: Short vowel sounds Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of KG English practice on short vowel sounds, from "Short a and e" to "Which Vowel?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Hear and write the short vowels a and e.
Hear and write the short vowels i, o and u.
Identify the short vowel in a word.

guide.what: The five short vowel sounds: a, e, i, o, u.
steps: Say each vowel with an action: a for apple, e for egg.
Say a short word slowly and ask which vowel is in the middle.
Change the vowel to make new words: cat, cot, cut.
home: Make words with fridge letters and swap the middle vowel.
Play vowel I Spy.
guide.watch: Short e and short i sound close. Exaggerate them: "e-e-egg", "i-i-itch".

title: CVC words Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of KG English practice on cvc words, from "Blend the Sounds" to "Read and Choose". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Blend three sounds to read and write a word.
Hear and match rhyming CVC words.
Read simple sentences with CVC words.

guide.what: Blending three sounds to read short words like cat, dog and sun.
steps: Say each sound slowly: c, a, t.
Say them faster until they join: cat.
Write the word and read it back.
home: Play robot talk: say "d-o-g" and let your child guess the word.
Build words with letter cards.
guide.watch: Some children add extra sounds ("cuh-a-tuh"). Keep each sound short and clipped.

title: Sight words Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of KG English practice on sight words, from "Trace the Sight Words" to "Find the Word". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read and write common sight words.
Use sight words to complete sentences.

guide.what: Common words children learn to read at a glance: the, and, is, I, to, can, see.
steps: Show the word on a card and read it together.
Find it in a story book.
Use it in a short spoken sentence.
home: Stick five sight word cards on the fridge and read them daily.
Play snap with sight word cards.
guide.watch: Sight words like "the" cannot be sounded out. Children learn them by seeing them often.

title: Numbers to 20 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on numbers to 20, from "Count and Write" to "Number Track". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Count objects to 20 and write the number.
Trace and say the teen numbers.

guide.what: Counting objects to 20 and reading and writing the numbers 11 to 20.
steps: Count real objects to 20, moving each one as you count.
Point out that 11 to 19 start with 1: one ten and some more.
Fill a number track together.
home: Count cars on the road up to 20.
Make a 1 to 20 number line on the floor with tape.
guide.watch: Teen numbers are tricky: we say "four" first in fourteen but write the 1 first.

title: More and less Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on more and less, from "Which Has More?" to "Biggest and Smallest". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Compare two groups and find which has more.
Find one more and one less than a number.

guide.what: Comparing groups and numbers: more, less, one more and one less.
steps: Make two groups of objects and ask which has more.
Line them up side by side to check.
Add one object and say "one more"; take one away and say "one less".
home: Compare biscuits on two plates.
On the stairs, one step up is one more, one step down is one less.
guide.watch: A long, spread-out line can look like more. Line objects up one-to-one to check.

title: Patterns Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on patterns, from "What Comes Next?" to "Make a Pattern". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Spotting, continuing and making simple repeating patterns.
steps: Make a pattern with spoons and forks: spoon, fork, spoon, fork.
Ask what comes next and why.
Let your child make a pattern for you to continue.
home: Clap and stamp patterns: clap, clap, stamp.
Thread beads in a colour pattern.
guide.watch: Some children copy the last item instead of the next. Say the pattern aloud together.

title: Seasons and weather Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on seasons and weather, from "Four Seasons" to "The Weather Today". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the four seasons and describe them.
Choose clothes for hot and cold weather.
Describe the weather and what we need for it.

guide.what: Naming the four seasons and the weather, and dressing for it.
steps: Look out of the window and describe the weather.
Talk about what we wear and eat in each season.
Keep a simple weather chart for a week.
home: Draw a sun, cloud or raindrop on the calendar each day.
Sort winter and summer clothes together.
guide.watch: Seasons feel abstract. Link each one to something your child remembers, like mangoes in summer.

title: Plants Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on plants, from "Parts of a Plant" to "Fruits and Vegetables". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the parts of a plant.
Know what plants need to grow.

guide.what: Parts of a plant and what plants need to grow.
steps: Look at a real plant and name its parts.
Plant a seed and talk about water and sunlight.
Sort fruits and vegetables in the kitchen.
home: Grow a chickpea or bean in wet cotton.
Water a plant together every day.
guide.watch: Children often forget roots are part of the plant. Pull up a weed to show them.

title: Community helpers Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on community helpers, from "Who Helps Us?" to "Who Would You Call?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name community helpers and their jobs.
Match helpers to the tools they use.
Know which helper to go to.

guide.what: The people who help us, the work they do and the tools they use.
steps: Talk about helpers you meet: the doctor, the shopkeeper, the sweeper.
Ask how each person helps us.
Role-play one job with toys.
home: Say thank you to a helper you meet this week.
Play doctor or shopkeeper at home.
guide.watch: Keep jobs open to everyone: girls and boys can be doctors, pilots and farmers.

title: حروفِ تہجی کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on the urdu alphabet (حروفِ تہجی), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Write the second half of the alphabet in order.
Find the first letter of a word.

guide.what: Saying and writing the Urdu alphabet in order.
steps: Sing the alphabet in order, pointing to each letter.
Cover a letter on a chart and ask which one is hiding.
Say a word and ask for its first letter.
home: Put alphabet cards in order on the floor.
Play "first letter": you say a word, your child says the letter.
guide.watch: Children rush through the middle of the alphabet. Practise in chunks of five or six letters.

title: دو حرفی الفاظ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on two-letter words (دو حرفی الفاظ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Join two letters to make a word.

guide.what: Joining two letters to read and write short words like دو، ہم، آم.
steps: Say each letter sound, then join them: د + و = دو.
Write the word and read it back.
Break the word apart again.
home: Make two-letter word cards and read three a day.
Find the word آم at the fruit shop.
guide.watch: Children may read letters separately without blending. Say the sounds faster until they join.

title: تین حرفی الفاظ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on three-letter words (تین حرفی الفاظ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Join three letters to make a word.

guide.what: Reading and writing three-letter words such as قلم، سیب، کان.
steps: Blend three sounds slowly: ق + ل + م.
Show how the letters join with their short forms.
Read the word in a short sentence.
home: Label things at home: قلم، سیب، کان.
Play "break the word" in the car.
guide.watch: When a naughty-nine letter is in the middle, the word breaks into parts. That is correct.

title: Numbers to 1000 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on numbers to 1000, from "Hundreds, Tens and Ones" to "Compare and Order". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read and write numbers to 1000 in words.

guide.what: Reading, writing and comparing numbers to 1000 using hundreds, tens and ones.
steps: Show 100 as ten bundles of 10 sticks.
Build a number like 345 with bundles and loose sticks.
Compare numbers by looking at the hundreds first.
home: Read prices in the bazaar and say how many hundreds.
Count in tens and hundreds while walking.
guide.watch: A zero in the middle (708) confuses children. Say "no tens" out loud.

title: Adding and subtracting Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on adding and subtracting, from "Add with Regrouping" to "Word Problems". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Solve addition and subtraction word problems.

guide.what: Adding and subtracting numbers up to 1000 when we need to carry or regroup.
steps: Use bundles of ten sticks to show 10 ones becoming 1 ten.
Write sums in columns, ones under ones.
Always start with the ones column.
home: Add two shop bills together.
Work out the change from 500 rupees.
guide.watch: In subtraction, children often take the smaller digit from the bigger one (52 − 27 = 35). Remind them to regroup when the top digit is smaller.

title: Multiplying by 2, 5 and 10 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on multiplying by 2, 5 and 10, from "Groups Of" to "Word Problems". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Multiplication as equal groups, and the 2, 5 and 10 times tables.
steps: Make equal groups of objects and count them.
Write it as repeated adding: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15.
Then write it as multiplying: 3 × 5 = 15.
home: Count money in 5 and 10 rupee coins.
Skip count in fives on the stairs.
guide.watch: Children sometimes add instead of multiply (3 × 5 = 8). Go back to drawing the groups.

title: Living and non-living Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on living and non-living, from "Living or Non-living?" to "What Living Things Need". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what all living things do.

guide.what: How we can tell living things from non-living things.
steps: List what living things do: grow, eat, breathe, move, have young.
Test objects against the list.
Talk about tricky ones: a car moves but does not grow.
home: Go on a living and non-living hunt in the garden.
Watch a plant grow over a week.
guide.watch: Children think anything that moves is alive (clouds, cars). Use the full list, not just movement.

title: Plants Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on plants, from "Parts and Jobs" to "Plant Experiment". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what each part of a plant does.
Order the stages of plant growth.
Explain what plants need from a simple test.

guide.what: Plant parts, what each part does, and how a plant grows from a seed.
steps: Pull up a small weed and look at its roots.
Put a white flower in coloured water and watch the stem carry it up.
Plant seeds and record growth each day.
home: Grow beans in a clear glass to see the roots.
Measure your plant every two days.
guide.watch: Children think plants eat soil. Explain that leaves make food using sunlight.

title: Animal habitats Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on animal habitats, from "Where Do They Live?" to "Made for Their Home". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Explain how animals are suited to their habitat.

guide.what: A habitat is where an animal lives, and animals have body parts that suit their home.
steps: Name an animal and ask where it lives.
Talk about what the habitat gives it: food, water, shelter.
Find one body part that helps it live there.
home: Watch a nature programme and name the habitats.
At the zoo, find animals from the desert, sea and forest.
guide.watch: Avoid saying animals choose their homes. Their bodies suit the place they live.

title: Early people Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 History practice on early people, from "How Early People Lived" to "Cave Painting". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Describe how the first people lived.
Compare life long ago with life today.
Use art to show what early people valued.

guide.what: How the first people found food, made tools and lived together.
steps: Ask: How would you live without shops or electricity?
Compare a stone tool with a knife at home.
Make a simple then-and-now chart.
home: Make a cave painting on brown paper.
Try grinding grain between two stones.
guide.watch: Early history covers a very long time. A simple timeline from long ago to now helps.

title: The Indus Valley Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 History practice on the indus valley, from "Mohenjo-daro" to "Design a Seal". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Describe the Indus Valley city of Mohenjo-daro.
Recall facts about Indus Valley life.
Learn about Indus seals through art.

guide.what: The Indus Valley people of Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, one of the world's first cities, here in Pakistan.
steps: Find the Indus River and Sindh on a map of Pakistan.
Look at pictures of the brick streets and the Great Bath.
Compare their homes with ours.
home: Build a brick house with blocks or clay.
Visit a museum or watch a short video about Mohenjo-daro.
guide.watch: Children may think the city is still lived in. Explain that people now visit its ruins.

title: Ancient Egypt Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 History practice on ancient egypt, from "Life by the Nile" to "Picture Writing". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Describe how Ancient Egyptians lived by the Nile.
Learn key words about Ancient Egypt.
Try picture writing like the Egyptians.

guide.what: How the people of Ancient Egypt lived by the Nile, their kings and their pyramids.
steps: Find Egypt and the Nile on a world map.
Compare the Nile with the Indus: both rivers helped farming.
Look at hieroglyphs and invent picture writing.
home: Build a pyramid from sugar cubes or blocks.
Write a secret message in picture writing.
guide.watch: Keep mummies simple and not scary: it was a way to honour people who had died.

title: Maps and directions Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on maps and directions, from "North, South, East, West" to "Draw a Map". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Draw a simple map with a key.

guide.what: Reading simple maps, using a key, and the four directions.
steps: Show a map of your area on a phone and find your home.
Stand outside and point to where the sun rises: east.
Draw a bird's-eye map of a room together.
home: Hide a treat and give directions to find it.
Draw the way from home to school.
guide.watch: Children mix up left and right with east and west. Directions stay the same when you turn around.

title: Continents and oceans Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on continents and oceans, from "Seven Continents" to "Animals Around the World". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Link animals to the continents where they live.

guide.what: The seven continents and five oceans, and where Pakistan is on the globe.
steps: Find Pakistan on a globe or world map.
Trace each continent with a finger and say its name.
Colour the oceans blue on a printed map.
home: Sing a continents song.
Pick a country each week and find it on the map.
guide.watch: Flat maps make sizes look wrong. Use a globe when you can.

title: Provinces of Pakistan Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on provinces of pakistan, from "Our Provinces" to "Map of Pakistan". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the provinces of Pakistan and their capitals.
Recall key facts about Pakistan's land.
Locate your own city on a map of Pakistan.

guide.what: The provinces of Pakistan, their capitals, and where we live.
steps: Look at a map of Pakistan and trace each province.
Say each capital and find it.
Mark your own city and the cities where relatives live.
home: Plan a pretend trip from Karachi to Gilgit.
Cook or taste a dish from another province.
guide.watch: Children may think the capital is Karachi or Lahore. Remind them it is Islamabad.

title: واحد جمع کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on singular and plural (واحد جمع), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Write the plural of Urdu nouns.
Write the singular of Urdu nouns.
Use singular and plural correctly in sentences.

guide.what: Singular means one, plural means more than one: کتاب، کتابیں.
steps: Show one object and then many, and say both words.
Point out common endings: ا becomes ے, ی becomes یاں.
Note words that stay the same, like پھول.
home: Count things at home and say the plural.
Play "one or many" with toys.
guide.watch: Some words do not change (پھول، گھر). Learn them as special words.

title: مذکر مؤنث کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on masculine and feminine (مذکر مؤنث), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Write feminine forms of Urdu nouns.
Write masculine forms of Urdu nouns.
Sort nouns as masculine or feminine.

guide.what: Words for males and females: لڑکا، لڑکی; دادا، دادی.
steps: Start with family words the child knows: امی، ابو.
Show the pattern: ا often becomes ی.
Sort word cards into two groups.
home: Name family members and say if each word is مذکر or مؤنث.
Play animal pairs: شیر، شیرنی.
guide.watch: Some pairs are completely different words (ماں، باپ). Learn these as pairs.

title: متضاد الفاظ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on opposites (متضاد الفاظ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Write opposites of common Urdu words.

guide.what: Words with opposite meanings: دن، رات; اوپر، نیچے.
steps: Act out opposites: stand up, sit down.
Say a word and let your child say its opposite.
Use both words in one sentence.
home: Find opposites at home: hot and cold water, open and closed doors.
Play opposites ping-pong in the car.
guide.watch: Some words have more than one opposite. Accept any sensible answer.

title: Multiplication and division Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on multiplication and division, from "Times Tables 3 and 4" to "Word Problems". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Solve multiplication and division word problems.

guide.what: Multiplying and dividing with the 3 and 4 times tables, and how the two are linked.
steps: Show 3 × 4 as 3 rows of 4 objects.
Share the same objects into equal groups to show division.
Write the fact family: 3 × 4, 4 × 3, 12 ÷ 3, 12 ÷ 4.
home: Share fruit equally among the family.
Arrange cups or chairs in rows and count them.
guide.watch: Division can mean "how many in each group" or "how many groups". Act out both.

title: Fractions Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on fractions, from "Halves, Thirds, Quarters" to "Compare Fractions". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Find halves, thirds and quarters of numbers.
Compare unit fractions and solve problems.

guide.what: Equal parts of a whole: halves, thirds and quarters, and finding a fraction of a number.
steps: Fold paper into equal parts and name them.
Cut a roti into halves and quarters.
Share objects equally to find ½ or ¼ of a number.
home: Share a pizza or roti into equal pieces.
Use measuring cups: half and quarter.
guide.watch: Children think a bigger bottom number means a bigger fraction (¼ > ½). Fold paper to compare.

title: Bar models Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on bar models, from "Part-Whole Bar Models" to "Two-Step Problems". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Drawing bar models to see what a word problem is asking, before doing the sum.
steps: Read the problem and draw one bar for the whole.
Split the bar into the parts you know and mark the missing part with ?.
Decide whether you are finding a part or the whole, then add or subtract.
home: Turn shopping trips into bar model problems.
Let your child draw the bar before you check the answer.
guide.watch: Children grab the numbers and add them. The bar picture shows when to subtract instead.

title: The human body Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on the human body, from "Organs and Their Jobs" to "Body Facts". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name main organs and what they do.
Choose habits that keep the body healthy.
Recall facts about bones, muscles and organs.

guide.what: Main organs, what they do, and habits that keep the body healthy.
steps: Feel your heartbeat before and after running.
Breathe deeply and feel your chest rise.
Talk about food, sleep, water and exercise.
home: Count your pulse for 15 seconds.
Plan a healthy plate together.
guide.watch: Keep it simple and positive. Avoid scary talk about illness.

title: Forces and magnets Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on forces and magnets, from "Push or Pull?" to "Magnet Facts". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort materials as magnetic or not.
Recall facts about magnets and friction.

guide.what: Forces are pushes and pulls; magnets pull some metals.
steps: Push and pull toys and watch how they move.
Test objects with a fridge magnet.
Slide a toy on carpet and on tiles to feel friction.
home: Magnet hunt in the kitchen.
Roll a ball on different floors and compare.
guide.watch: Not all metals are magnetic (steel yes, aluminium foil no). Test, do not guess.

title: States of matter Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on states of matter, from "Solid, Liquid or Gas?" to "Properties". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort materials into solids, liquids and gases.
Compare the properties of solids, liquids and gases.

guide.what: Solids, liquids and gases, and how heating and cooling change them.
steps: Look at ice, water and the steam from a kettle (safely).
Ask: does it keep its shape? Can you pour it?
Freeze water and melt it again.
home: Make ice lollies from juice.
Watch the mirror go misty after a hot bath.
guide.watch: Visible steam is tiny water drops; real water vapour is invisible. At this age, "steam" is fine.

title: Mesopotamia Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 History practice on mesopotamia, from "Land Between Two Rivers" to "Then and Now". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Describe where Mesopotamia was and what it gave us.
Link ancient inventions to life today.

guide.what: Mesopotamia, one of the first places to build cities, and its inventions like writing and the wheel.
steps: Find Iraq and the two rivers on a map.
Compare it with the Indus: both grew beside rivers.
Press marks into clay to try cuneiform.
home: Make a clay tablet and write your name in wedge marks.
List all the wheels you see in one day.
guide.watch: A timeline helps: Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley lived at about the same time.

title: Ancient China Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 History practice on ancient china, from "Gifts from China" to "The Silk Road". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Explain how the Silk Road linked China and our region.

guide.what: Ancient China and its inventions, and the Silk Road that linked it to our part of the world.
steps: Find China on the map next to Pakistan.
Talk about inventions we still use: paper, kites, the compass.
Trace the Silk Road through the Karakoram mountains.
home: Make a paper kite.
Taste green tea and talk about where tea came from.
guide.watch: Keep dates simple: "a very long time ago" is fine for Grade 3.

title: Gandhara Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 History practice on gandhara, from "The Land of Gandhara" to "A Museum Visit". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Describe the ancient kingdom of Gandhara.

guide.what: Gandhara, an ancient kingdom in north-west Pakistan, its art and the old learning centre of Taxila.
steps: Find Taxila, Peshawar and Swat on a map of Pakistan.
Look at photos of Gandhara stone carvings.
Talk about why people travelled far to learn at Taxila.
home: Visit the Taxila Museum or the Lahore Museum if you can.
Carve a simple shape in a bar of soap with a blunt tool.
guide.watch: Present Gandhara as part of Pakistan's shared heritage that we look after.

title: Landforms and water Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Geography practice on landforms and water, from "Landforms" to "Landforms of Pakistan". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name kinds of water bodies with examples from Pakistan.

guide.what: The shapes of land and water on Earth, with examples from Pakistan.
steps: Make a landform model with sand or clay, then pour water to make a river.
Look at photos of Pakistan's mountains, deserts and plains.
Find each one on a physical map.
home: Point out landforms on trips: hills, rivers, plains.
Draw a map of an imaginary island with landforms.
guide.watch: Valleys and plains are both low, but a valley sits between hills or mountains.

title: Weather and climate Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Geography practice on weather and climate, from "Weather Words" to "Weather Diary". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Weather is what the sky is like today; climate is the usual weather of a place over many years.
steps: Look at the sky each morning and describe it.
Read a weather forecast together.
Compare the climate of Murree and Karachi.
home: Keep a weather diary for a week.
Make a rain gauge from a plastic bottle.
guide.watch: Children mix up weather and climate. Weather changes daily; climate is the pattern.

title: Pakistan and its neighbours Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Geography practice on pakistan and its neighbours, from "Our Neighbours" to "Map Work". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name Pakistan's neighbours and their directions.
Show Pakistan's borders on a map.

guide.what: The countries and sea that border Pakistan, and their directions.
steps: Find Pakistan on a map of Asia.
Go round the border and name each neighbour.
Use compass directions to describe where each one is.
home: Find the neighbours on a globe.
Talk about foods or words we share with neighbours.
guide.watch: Keep the focus on geography and friendly links, not politics.

title: اسم کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on nouns (اسم), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Sort nouns into person, place and thing.

guide.what: An اسم is the name of a person, place or thing.
steps: Point to things around the house and say their names as nouns.
Sort word cards into person, place and thing.
Find nouns in a short Urdu story.
home: Play "name ten things in the kitchen".
Underline nouns in a newspaper headline.
guide.watch: Children sometimes pick adjectives (بڑا) as nouns. Ask: is it the name of something?

title: فعل کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on verbs (فعل), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Identify past, present and future verbs.

guide.what: A فعل is an action word. Verbs also show when something happens: past, present or future.
steps: Act out actions and name them: دوڑنا، کھانا، لکھنا.
Find the verb at the end of an Urdu sentence.
Say one action in the past, present and future.
home: Play "what are you doing?" and answer in Urdu.
Tell the story of yesterday using past-tense verbs.
guide.watch: In Urdu the verb usually comes at the end of the sentence. Look there first.

title: صفت کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on adjectives (صفت), with an answer key for every page.

guide.what: A صفت describes a noun: its colour, size, taste or quality.
steps: Hold an object and ask: یہ کیسا ہے؟
List describing words on paper.
Add a صفت to make a sentence more interesting.
home: Describe dinner with Urdu adjectives.
Play "I am thinking of something red and round" in Urdu.
guide.watch: Adjectives ending in ا change with the noun (بڑا لڑکا، بڑی لڑکی). Point this out gently.

title: Talking words Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Nursery English practice on talking words, from "Big and Small" to "Magic Words". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use the size words big and small.
Hear and point to the words in, on and under.
Use courtesy words at the right time.

guide.what: Everyday talking words: big and small, in, on and under, and polite words like please and thank you.
steps: Say the word while showing it: put a toy on the table, then under it.
Ask your child to copy you: "Put the spoon in the cup."
Model magic words all day and praise your child when they use one.
home: Play "Simon says" with in, on and under.
Sort toys into a big pile and a small pile.
guide.watch: Young children understand many more words than they can say. Keep talking in short, clear sentences.

title: First sounds s a t p Practice
topic: First sounds s a t p
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Nursery English practice on first sounds s a t p, from "Trace s a t p" to "Same Sound?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Trace the letters s, a, t and p and say their sounds.
Hear the first sound in a word.
Hear when two words start with the same sound.

pages.title: Trace s a t p
pages.topic: First sounds s a t p

pages.title: Which Sound First?
pages.topic: First sounds s a t p

pages.title: Same Sound?
pages.topic: First sounds s a t p

guide.what: The sounds s, a, t and p, the first letters children learn because they make many small words.
steps: Say the sound, not the letter name: "sss" like a snake.
Show something that starts with the sound, like a sock.
Trace the letter in the air, then on paper.
home: Play I Spy with sounds: "I spy something that starts with sss."
Make a sound basket of things that start with s.
guide.watch: Avoid adding "uh" to sounds (say "t", not "tuh"). Clipped sounds make blending easier later.

title: Nursery rhymes Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Nursery English practice on nursery rhymes, from "Twinkle, Twinkle" to "Rhyme Time". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Recite a rhyme and hear rhyming words.
Answer simple questions about a rhyme.

guide.what: Saying rhymes aloud helps children hear sounds in words, the first step towards reading.
steps: Say the rhyme slowly with actions.
Stop before the last word and let your child finish it.
Clap along to feel the beat.
home: Sing one rhyme at bath time and one at bedtime.
Make up silly rhymes with names: Ali, Pali, Mali.
guide.watch: Children love repeating the same rhyme many times. That repetition is exactly how they learn.

title: Listen and answer Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Nursery English practice on listen and answer, from "Moti's Bone" to "What Comes First?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Answer simple questions about a story read aloud.
Recall the characters and events of a story.

guide.what: Listening to short stories and answering who, what and where questions about them.
steps: Read the story twice: once for fun, once to answer the questions.
Point to the words as you read, left to right.
Ask one question at a time and wait for an answer.
home: Read one picture book every night and ask: Who was in the story?
Retell a story using toys.
guide.watch: If your child cannot answer, read the sentence with the answer again. Do not give the answer straight away.

title: Draw and tell Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Nursery English practice on draw and tell, from "My Favourite Fruit" to "My Family". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Draw a picture and talk about it.
Trace short words with correct letter shapes.

guide.what: Drawing and talking are a child's first writing: they tell a story with pictures and words.
steps: Ask your child to tell you about the picture.
Write their words under it and read them back.
Praise the idea, not the neatness.
home: Keep a scrapbook of drawings with your child's words written underneath.
Draw something you did today together.
guide.watch: Scribbles that "say" something are real early writing. Ask "What does it say?" instead of "What is it?"

title: Position and comparing Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of KG English practice on position and comparing, from "Where Is It?" to "Days of the Week". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use the position words in, on, under, above and below.
Say and order the days of the week.

guide.what: Position words, comparing words with -er and -est, and the days of the week.
steps: Act it out: put a toy above, below, in and on things.
Line up three things and say big, bigger, biggest.
Sing the days of the week each morning.
home: Ask: Which day is it today? Which day was yesterday?
Compare family heights: who is taller?
guide.watch: Children may say "more bigger". Repeat it back correctly: "Yes, it is bigger!"

title: Sounds sh, ch, th Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of KG English practice on sounds sh, ch, th, from "sh or ch?" to "Read and Match". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Hear the digraphs sh and ch at the start of words.
Write sh, ch and th in words.
Read words with sh, ch and th.

guide.what: Two letters can make one sound: sh as in ship, ch as in chair, th as in thumb.
steps: Show that s and h together make a new sound, "shh" like a quiet finger.
Say ch like a train: ch, ch, ch.
Stick out your tongue a little for th.
home: Hunt for sh, ch and th words on food packets.
Play "quiet sh, loud ch" with picture cards.
guide.watch: Children often say "f" for th (fumb). Show them the tongue between the teeth in a mirror.

title: Rhymes and rhyming words Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of KG English practice on rhymes and rhyming words, from "Hickory Dickory Dock" to "Hot Cross Buns". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read a rhyme and find rhyming words.
Recall the words of a rhyme.

guide.what: Rhyming words end with the same sound, like cat and hat. Rhymes help children read word families.
steps: Say the rhyme and clap the beat.
Ask: Which words sound the same at the end?
Change the first sound to make new rhymes: cat, hat, bat, mat.
home: Play rhyme ping-pong: you say "cat", your child says "hat".
Sing a rhyme in the car and leave out the last word.
guide.watch: Nonsense rhymes count! "Cat, zat" shows your child hears the pattern.

title: Read and answer Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of KG English practice on read and answer, from "Sam and the Cat" to "Story Order". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read short sentences and answer questions.
Read a short story and check facts.

guide.what: Reading short sentences made of simple words, then answering questions about them.
steps: Read the story aloud first, pointing to each word.
Let your child read it back to you.
Ask the questions out loud before they circle.
home: Read shop signs and labels together.
After a story, ask what happened first, next and last.
guide.watch: Guessing words from pictures is normal. Gently point back to the letters and blend them.

title: Writing words Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of KG English practice on writing words, from "Missing Letter" to "All About Me". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Write the middle sound in CVC words.
Copy short sentences with a capital and a full stop.
Write your name and simple facts about yourself.

guide.what: Writing short words and simple sentences with spaces, capitals and full stops.
steps: Say the word slowly and hear each sound: c-a-t.
Write one letter for each sound.
Leave a finger space between words.
home: Write a shopping list together: egg, jam, bun.
Let your child write labels for their toys.
guide.watch: Spelling by sound ("bus" as "bs") is a normal step. Praise the sounds they got right.

title: Shapes and lines Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on shapes and lines, from "Flat Shapes" to "Straight or Curved?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Count sides and corners of 2D shapes.
Name 3D shapes: cube, sphere, cylinder, cone.
Tell straight lines from curved lines.

guide.what: Naming flat and solid shapes and describing them by sides, corners and lines.
steps: Feel a box and count its corners.
Roll a ball and a box: which one rolls?
Look for straight and curved lines in the room.
home: Find a cylinder, a sphere and a cube in the kitchen.
Build towers with boxes and tins.
guide.watch: A cube and a square are different: a cube is solid and has 6 square faces.

title: Money Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on money, from "Pakistani Coins and Notes" to "At the Shop". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Decide if there is enough money to buy something.

guide.what: Recognising Pakistani rupee coins and notes, adding small amounts and shopping.
steps: Let your child hold and name each coin.
Play shop with real or toy coins.
Count coins starting with the biggest value.
home: Let your child pay at a small shop with your help.
Set up a pretend tuck shop at home.
guide.watch: A bigger coin is not always worth more. Teach the number on it, not the size.

title: Time Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on time, from "O'Clock" to "My Day". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell the time to the hour.
Tell the time to the half hour.

guide.what: Telling the time to the hour and half hour, and the parts of the day.
steps: Show a real clock: the short hand is the hour, the long hand the minutes.
At o'clock, the long hand points straight up to 12.
At half past, the long hand points straight down to 6.
home: Ask your child to tell you when it is 5 o'clock.
Make a paper plate clock together.
guide.watch: Children mix up the two hands. Say "the short hand is short of time, it moves slowly".

title: My body and senses Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on my body and senses, from "Body Parts" to "Look After Your Body". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name body parts and what they do.
Match actions to the five senses.

guide.what: Naming body parts and the five senses, and keeping our bodies healthy.
steps: Play "Simon says touch your..."
Do a blindfold taste test with safe foods.
Talk about why we sleep and exercise.
home: Make a daily healthy habits chart.
Go on a sense walk: what can you hear, see and smell?
guide.watch: Children may think the heart is on the left of the chest only. It is in the middle, tilted slightly left.

title: Healthy food Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on healthy food, from "Healthy or Not?" to "Where Does It Come From?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell everyday healthy foods from treats.
Sort foods into fruits, vegetables and grains.
Know that food comes from plants and animals.

guide.what: Healthy food, food groups and where our food comes from.
steps: Name the foods on your plate and their groups.
Talk about why treats are for sometimes.
Visit a vegetable stall and name everything.
home: Let your child help pack a healthy lunch.
Grow a small plant like mint or coriander.
guide.watch: Avoid calling foods "good" or "bad". Say "everyday foods" and "sometimes foods".

title: Materials around us Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on materials around us, from "What Is It Made Of?" to "Floats or Sinks?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Describe materials as hard or soft.
Predict and test if things float or sink.

guide.what: Things are made of materials like wood, metal, glass, plastic and cloth, each with its own properties.
steps: Touch things and describe them: hard, soft, smooth, rough.
Ask: Why is a window made of glass?
Test things in a tub of water.
home: Sort kitchen things by material.
Make a float or sink chart.
guide.watch: A heavy ship floats because of its shape. For now, just test and talk about what happens.

title: My school Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on my school, from "People at School" to "All About My School". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name people who work at school.

guide.what: The people at school, school rules and our own school.
steps: Talk about your child's school day: who did you meet?
Ask why each school rule matters.
Say thank you to school staff together.
home: Make a card for a teacher or the school guard.
Pack the school bag together the night before.
guide.watch: Some children feel shy at school. Ask about one happy moment each day.

title: Community helpers Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on community helpers, from "Who Helps Us?" to "Thank You, Helpers". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know when to call for help.

guide.what: People in the community who help us, where they work and how to ask for help.
steps: Point out helpers when you are out: the sweeper, the traffic warden.
Ask: What would happen without farmers?
Learn emergency numbers together.
home: Role play being a doctor or shopkeeper.
Give a cold drink to a worker on a hot day.
guide.watch: Every job deserves respect. Talk about sweepers and cleaners as important helpers too.

title: Pakistan, my country Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on pakistan, my country, from "National Symbols" to "Our Leaders". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the national symbols of Pakistan.

guide.what: Pakistan's national symbols, national days and founders.
steps: Show the national symbols on a poster or online.
Talk about why we celebrate 14 August.
Find Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad on a map.
home: Learn a national song.
Visit Minar-e-Pakistan, Mazar-e-Quaid or Faisal Mosque if you can.
guide.watch: Keep history simple at this age: Pakistan was made so people could live freely.

title: Numbers in order Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on numbers in order, from "Count and Write" to "Before and After". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Count objects to 10 and write the number.
Say and write numbers 1 to 10 in order.
Find the number just before and just after.

guide.what: Counting objects to 10 and saying numbers in the right order.
steps: Count stairs, buttons or rotis, touching each one.
Count forwards and backwards from 10 like a rocket launch.
Ask: What comes after 4?
home: Count the cars on the road on the way to school.
Play hopscotch with numbers 1 to 10.
guide.watch: Children often skip or repeat numbers when counting. Touching each object once fixes this.

title: Sorting and matching Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on sorting and matching, from "More or Fewer?" to "Sort by Colour". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Compare two groups and find the one with more.
See when two groups have the same number.

guide.what: Sorting things into groups and comparing groups to see which has more.
steps: Sort laundry: socks in one pile, shirts in another.
Line up two groups side by side to see which is longer.
Use words: more, fewer, the same.
home: Sort buttons or blocks by colour and size.
Share sweets equally and check both have the same.
guide.watch: Bigger objects can look like "more". Line them up one-to-one to check.

title: Long, short, heavy, light Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on long, short, heavy, light, from "Long or Short?" to "Heavy or Light?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Compare length using long and short.
Compare height using tall and short.
Compare weight using heavy and light.

guide.what: Comparing things by length, height and weight.
steps: Hold two things and ask: Which is heavier?
Line up pencils from short to long.
Stand back to back and see who is taller.
home: Weigh fruit at the market with your hands first, then the scale.
Measure your child against a door frame.
guide.watch: Big things are not always heavy (a balloon). Let your child feel the weight.

title: Fruits and vegetables Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on fruits and vegetables, from "Fruit or Vegetable?" to "My Favourite". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the colours of fruits and vegetables.

guide.what: Naming fruits and vegetables and their colours.
steps: Take your child to the fruit and vegetable stall and name everything.
Let your child touch, smell and taste.
Sort fruits and vegetables at home.
home: Make a fruit chaat together.
Play "I spy something yellow" in the kitchen.
guide.watch: Tomatoes are really a fruit, but we cook them like vegetables. Either answer is fine at this age.

title: My home Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on my home, from "Rooms of the House" to "My Family". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Draw and talk about home and family.

guide.what: Rooms of a house, things in them, and the people who live at home.
steps: Walk around the house and name each room.
Ask: What do we do in the kitchen?
Talk about who lives in your home.
home: Let your child help tidy one room.
Play house with toys.
guide.watch: Homes are different. Some families share rooms. Talk about your home without comparing.

title: Transport Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on transport, from "Land, Water or Air?" to "Draw a Ride". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort transport by land, water and air.

guide.what: Ways we travel on land, water and in the air.
steps: Name vehicles you see on the road.
Count wheels on cars, bikes and rickshaws.
Talk about road safety: hold hands when crossing.
home: Play "stop and go" with red and green cards.
Make a boat from paper and float it.
guide.watch: Every trip is a chance to talk about safety: seatbelts, helmets and holding hands.

title: حروف اور تصویریں کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on letters and pictures (حروف اور تصویریں), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Hear the first letter of Urdu words.
Match letters to words that start with them.
Trace Urdu letters and say their sounds.

guide.what: Hearing the first letter of Urdu words and matching letters to pictures.
steps: Say the word slowly and stress the first sound.
Show a real object for each letter.
Trace the letter with a finger, then a pencil.
home: Play I Spy in Urdu: "میں ایک چیز دیکھ رہا ہوں جو ب سے شروع ہوتی ہے".
Make a letter book with drawings.
guide.watch: Some letters sound alike (س، ص، ث). At this age, teach the most common one first.

title: رنگ اور گنتی کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on colours and counting (رنگ اور گنتی), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Know the colours of everyday things in Urdu.
Say and write Urdu numbers 1 to 5.

guide.what: Colours and counting from one to five in Urdu.
steps: Name colours in Urdu during the day.
Count steps in Urdu: ایک، دو، تین.
Match colour cards to things at home.
home: Sort clothes by colour and name them in Urdu.
Count rotis at dinner in Urdu.
guide.watch: Many families mix Urdu and English colour names. Both are fine; repeat the Urdu word often.

title: ننھی نظمیں کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on little rhymes (ننھی نظمیں), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Draw a picture for a rhyme.

guide.what: Saying traditional Urdu rhymes and hearing words that rhyme.
steps: Say the rhyme with hand actions.
Pause and let your child finish the line.
Clap the beat together.
home: Sing the rhyme at bath time.
Make up a rhyme about your cat or bird.
guide.watch: Rhymes build listening skills for reading Urdu. Repeat them many times.

title: Adding to 10 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on adding to 10, from "Add the Shapes" to "Make 10". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Add two small groups by counting.

guide.what: Putting two groups together and counting all of them to add.
steps: Use real things: 3 spoons and 2 spoons, how many?
Say the sum as a sentence: 3 and 2 make 5.
Use fingers to make 10.
home: Add plates while setting the dastarkhwan.
Play dice games and add the dots.
guide.watch: Children may count everything from 1 each time. Show them to start from the bigger number and count on.

title: Taking away Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on taking away, from "Take Away" to "Add or Take Away?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Take away from a small group.
Choose whether a story needs adding or taking away.

guide.what: Taking away means some go, and we count how many are left.
steps: Act it out: 5 toys, hide 2, how many are left?
Say: 5 take away 2 leaves 3.
Use "left" and "fewer" in everyday talk.
home: Count rotis before and after dinner.
Sing "Five Little Ducks" and take one away each verse.
guide.watch: The minus sign is new. Call it "take away" until your child is confident.

title: Shapes all around Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on shapes all around, from "Name the Shape" to "Count the Sides". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Count the sides of flat shapes.

guide.what: Naming flat shapes, finding them around us and counting their sides.
steps: Go on a shape walk around the house.
Trace the sides of a shape with a finger and count.
Make shapes with sticks or straws.
home: Cut sandwiches into triangles and squares.
Draw pictures using only shapes.
guide.watch: A square is a special rectangle. At this age, just notice that a square's sides are all the same.

title: Healthy habits and safety Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on healthy habits and safety, from "Healthy Habits" to "Emergency Numbers". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know who to call in an emergency.

guide.what: Healthy habits and simple safety rules at home and outside.
steps: Make hand washing fun: sing while you scrub for 20 seconds.
Practise crossing the road: stop, look, listen.
Learn emergency numbers by heart.
home: Make a bedtime routine chart.
Role play: what to do if you get lost in a market.
guide.watch: Teach "safe strangers": a police officer or a shopkeeper at the counter.

title: Animals and their young Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on animals and their young, from "Baby Animals" to "Pet or Wild?". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Baby animals, animal homes, and pets and wild animals.
steps: Look at animals at a farm or zoo and name their babies.
Talk about how to be gentle with pets.
Read an animal picture book.
home: Visit a nearby farm or park with ducks.
Feed birds on the roof with grain and water.
guide.watch: Many animal babies have special names. A few just add "baby", and that is fine too.

title: Our country Pakistan Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on our country pakistan, from "Our Flag" to "Our Hero". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Simple facts about Pakistan: the flag, capital, language, national symbols and heroes.
steps: Look at the flag together and name its colours and shapes.
Sing the national anthem or a national song.
Show Pakistan on a map or globe.
home: Decorate your home on 14 August.
Find the flag on coins and notes.
guide.watch: Children enjoy national symbols. Keep facts short and add one new fact a week.

title: زبر، زیر، پیش کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on short vowel marks (زبر، زیر، پیش), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read two-letter words with vowel marks.
Choose words with the right vowel marks.

guide.what: The short vowel marks زبر، زیر and پیش and how they change the sound.
steps: Show zabar as a little line above: mouth opens wide.
Zer is a line below: smile.
Pesh is like a small و above: round lips.
home: Move your hand up for zabar, down for zer and forward for pesh.
Read short words on shop signs together.
guide.watch: Most Urdu books drop vowel marks later. Children need them while learning, so keep them in.

title: نظم: ہماری گائے کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on poem: our cow (نظم: ہماری گائے), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read a classic Urdu poem for children.
Know what we get from a cow.
Find rhyming words in a poem.

guide.what: Reading a classic poem by Ismail Merathi and talking about what a cow gives us.
steps: Read the poem aloud and let your child repeat each line.
Talk about milk, yogurt and butter.
Find the rhyming words.
home: Visit a dairy or farm.
Make lassi together and talk about where milk comes from.
guide.watch: Ismail Merathi wrote many poems for children over a hundred years ago. They are still loved today.

title: جملے پڑھنا کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on reading sentences (جملے پڑھنا), with an answer key for every page.

guide.what: Reading and writing short Urdu sentences.
steps: Point to each word as you read together.
Ask a simple question after each sentence.
Praise neat letters and spaces.
home: Write a short Urdu note for your child each day.
Read Urdu signs in the market.
guide.watch: Joining letters is the hardest part. Let your child read aloud before writing.

title: Money and shopping Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on money and shopping, from "Count the Money" to "Bazaar Problems". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Add Pakistani money up to Rs 1000.

guide.what: Adding money, working out change and solving shopping problems with rupees.
steps: Count money from the biggest note to the smallest.
Count up to find change: 70 + 30 = 100.
Write money with Rs before the number.
home: Let your child check the bill at a shop.
Give a small budget for the tuck shop and plan spending.
guide.watch: Adding money is just adding numbers. Remind your child to line up the digits.

title: Time and calendar Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on time and calendar, from "Quarter Past and To" to "Reading a Calendar". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell the time to the quarter hour.
Read days and months on a calendar.

guide.what: Telling the time to the quarter hour and reading a calendar.
steps: At quarter past, the long hand points to 3. At quarter to, it points to 9.
Count in fives around the clock.
Find important dates on a wall calendar.
home: Ask your child to tell you the time each evening.
Mark birthdays and holidays on a calendar.
guide.watch: "Quarter to" is tricky because the hour has not come yet. Practise with a real clock.

title: Length, mass and capacity Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on length, mass and capacity, from "Which Unit?" to "Heavier or Lighter?". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Measuring length in metres, mass in kilograms and capacity in litres.
steps: Measure a room with a measuring tape.
Read the kg on packets of rice and flour.
Fill a bottle with water and count the litres.
home: Weigh fruit together at the shop.
Measure your height every month.
guide.watch: Big does not always mean heavy. Let your child hold things to compare.

title: Food and teeth Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on food and teeth, from "Food Groups" to "A Balanced Meal". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort foods into energy, body-building and protective foods.
Name types of teeth and care for them.

guide.what: Food groups, a balanced diet and how to look after our teeth.
steps: Look at a meal and name each food group.
Look in a mirror and find the different teeth.
Brush teeth together for two minutes.
home: Plan a balanced meal for the family together.
Make a brushing chart with stickers.
guide.watch: Milk teeth fall out from about age 6. It is normal, and the new teeth need extra care.

title: Water Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on water, from "Uses of Water" to "Save Water". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Describe the water cycle in steps.

guide.what: How we use water, the water cycle and why we must save water.
steps: Boil water and watch steam rise, then cool on a lid.
Count the ways your family uses water in a day.
Talk about why Pakistan needs to save water.
home: Put a bucket under the AC drain and use the water for plants.
Make a "save water" sign for the bathroom.
guide.watch: Children think clouds are smoke or cotton. Explain they are tiny drops of water.

title: Earth and sky Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on earth and sky, from "Day and Night" to "Shapes of the Moon". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what we see in the day and night sky.
Know simple facts about the Sun, Moon and Earth.
Notice that the Moon seems to change shape.

guide.what: The Sun, Moon and Earth, day and night, and the changing shape of the Moon.
steps: Shine a torch on a ball in a dark room and turn the ball slowly.
Go out at night and look at the Moon together.
Never look straight at the Sun.
home: Keep a Moon diary for a week.
Watch the sunrise or sunset together.
guide.watch: The Moon does not make its own light. It shines because sunlight falls on it.

title: Then and now Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 History practice on then and now, from "Past or Present?" to "Ask an Elder". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Compare life in the past and today.
Learn about the past from older people.
