guide.what: How life has changed over time, timelines, and learning history from elders.
steps: Look at old family photos together.
Draw a timeline of your child's life with photos.
Ask grandparents about their childhood.
home: Visit a museum such as Lahore Museum.
Find an old object at home and talk about it.
guide.watch: Children often think "long ago" means dinosaurs. Use family timelines to show recent history.

title: Quaid-e-Azam Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 History practice on quaid-e-azam, from "Life of the Quaid" to "Order the Events". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Order events in the Quaid's life.

guide.what: The life of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, founder of Pakistan, and his motto.
steps: Show a photo of the Quaid and talk about his life.
Discuss how the motto can be used at school.
Visit or look at pictures of Mazar-e-Quaid.
home: Celebrate 25 December with a story about the Quaid.
Make a poster of Unity, Faith, Discipline.
guide.watch: Keep it positive: he worked very hard and never gave up.

title: Cities and landmarks Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on cities and landmarks, from "Which City?" to "Port City". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know famous landmarks of Pakistan's cities.
Know the capital of Pakistan and its provinces.

guide.what: Famous cities and landmarks of Pakistan and the capitals of its provinces.
steps: Find each city on a map of Pakistan.
Look at photos of the landmarks together.
Talk about any city your family has visited.
home: Plan a pretend trip around Pakistan.
Make postcards of landmarks.
guide.watch: Karachi is the biggest city, but Islamabad is the capital. Children often mix these up.

title: Seasons in Pakistan Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on seasons in pakistan, from "Four Seasons" to "Hot and Cold Places". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Match clothes and activities to seasons.
Know that weather is different in different places.

guide.what: Pakistan's seasons and how weather changes from place to place.
steps: Talk about this season's weather and clothes.
Watch the weather forecast together.
Compare the weather in two cities.
home: Keep a weather chart for a week.
Collect leaves in autumn.
guide.watch: Seasons vary in Pakistan. The north gets snow while the south stays warm.

title: Villages and cities Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on villages and cities, from "Village or City?" to "Where I Live". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know jobs in villages and cities.
Describe your own village or city.

guide.what: How life in villages and cities is different and how they depend on each other.
steps: Look at photos of a village and a city and compare.
Ask: Where does our wheat and milk come from?
Talk about relatives who live in a village or city.
home: Visit a village or farm if you can.
Make a two-column list: village, city.
guide.watch: Villages and cities need each other: food comes from villages, many goods come from cities.

title: Rights and responsibilities Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on rights and responsibilities, from "Rights" to "Good Citizens". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know our responsibilities at home, school and in the community.
Explain how to be a good citizen.

guide.what: Rights are things everyone should have; responsibilities are things we should do.
steps: Talk about one right and one responsibility each day.
Give your child a small household responsibility.
Praise responsible choices.
home: Clean up a park or street with the family.
Make a family rules and responsibilities chart.
guide.watch: Rights and responsibilities go together. Ask: If you have a right to a clean park, what is your responsibility?

title: Festivals of Pakistan Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on festivals of pakistan, from "Which Festival?" to "My Favourite Festival". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the main festivals in Pakistan.

guide.what: The religious and national festivals celebrated in Pakistan, and respect for all faiths.
steps: Talk about how your family celebrates Eid.
Learn how friends of other faiths celebrate their festivals.
Make Eid cards together.
home: Help prepare a festival dish.
Wish neighbours on their festivals.
guide.watch: Pakistan has people of many faiths. Learning about all festivals builds respect.

title: فہمِ عبارت کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on reading for meaning (فہمِ عبارت), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Answer questions in full Urdu sentences.

guide.what: Reading an Urdu passage and answering questions in full sentences.
steps: Read the questions first, then the passage.
Underline the answer in the passage.
Start the answer with words from the question.
home: Read an Urdu children's magazine together.
Ask your child to tell you about their day in Urdu.
guide.watch: Full-sentence answers are a new skill. Show how to reuse the question's words.

words: ابو نے زینب کو عیدی دی۔
نانی نے شیر خرما بنایا تھا۔

title: نظم: ایک گائے اور بکری کی مشق
en: Poem: A Cow and a Goat practice
topicEn: Poem: A Cow and a Goat
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on poem: a cow and a goat (نظم: ایک گائے اور بکری), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Learn the meanings of words in the poem.

guide.what: Reading the opening of Iqbal's poem "Aik Gaye aur Bakri" and learning new words.
steps: Read the lines slowly and explain each word.
Look at a picture of a green meadow.
Find the rhyming words at the end of the lines.
home: Read the whole poem from an Iqbal children's book.
Visit a park and describe it in Urdu.
guide.watch: This poem has a lesson about being thankful. Read it all together over a week.

title: جملے اور کہانی کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on sentences and stories (جملے اور کہانی), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Order words to make a sentence.
Write a short story from word prompts.

guide.what: Making sentences and writing a short story in Urdu.
steps: Say the sentence aloud before writing.
Check that each sentence ends with ۔
Use first, then, at the end: پہلے، پھر، آخر میں.
home: Tell a story together in Urdu at bedtime.
Write a short Urdu diary entry once a week.
guide.watch: Spelling mistakes are normal. Praise complete sentences and good ideas first.

title: Measurement Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on measurement, from "Units of Length" to "Measurement Problems". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Convert grams and kilograms, millilitres and litres.

guide.what: Converting between units of length, mass and capacity, and solving measurement problems.
steps: Show 1 metre with a tape and count 100 cm.
Read grams and millilitres on food packets.
Use a measuring jug while cooking.
home: Measure ingredients together for a recipe.
Check the distance to school on a map app.
guide.watch: Children forget to change units before adding. Ask: Are both in metres?

title: Data handling Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on data handling, from "Pictograph" to "Bar Graph Questions". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read a pictograph with a key.
Answer questions from a data table.

guide.what: Reading and making pictographs, tally charts and simple tables.
steps: Make a tally of birds you see from the window.
Draw a pictograph with a key: each picture equals 2.
Ask questions: most, fewest, how many more?
home: Survey the family about favourite foods and make a chart.
Count cars by colour on a drive.
guide.watch: With a key, each picture may stand for more than one. Always read the key first.

title: Angles and perimeter Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on angles and perimeter, from "Right Angles" to "Lines". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know horizontal, vertical and parallel lines.

guide.what: Right angles, kinds of lines and finding the perimeter of shapes.
steps: Use the corner of a paper as a right angle checker.
Walk around a table and count the sides.
Look for parallel lines on railway tracks or notebook lines.
home: Measure the perimeter of a photo frame.
Find right angles around the house.
guide.watch: Perimeter is the distance around; area is the space inside. Use a fence and grass to explain.

title: Life cycles Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on life cycles, from "Butterfly Life Cycle" to "Plant Life Cycle". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Order the stages of a butterfly's life cycle.
Describe the life cycle of a frog.
Describe the life cycle of a flowering plant.

guide.what: Living things are born, grow, reproduce and die. Different living things have different life cycles.
steps: Grow a bean in a glass jar and watch each day.
Look at photos of yourself as a baby, toddler and now.
Compare animal babies with their parents.
home: Find a caterpillar on a plant and check on it.
Plant seeds from a fruit you ate.
guide.watch: Some young look like their parents (kittens); others do not (tadpoles). Talk about both.

title: Natural resources Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on natural resources, from "Natural or Man-made?" to "Pollution". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell natural resources from man-made things.
Know types of pollution and how to reduce them.

guide.what: Natural resources like water, air, soil and wood, pollution, and the 3 Rs.
steps: Make a list of natural resources you used today.
Sort household waste into paper, plastic and food.
Talk about smog in winter and why it happens.
home: Plant a tree for your birthday.
Make a toy from boxes and bottles.
guide.watch: Recycling is good, but reducing is best. Start with saying no to extra plastic bags.

title: The Sun and shadows Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on the sun and shadows, from "The Solar System" to "Directions". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know simple facts about the solar system.
Explain how shadows form and change.

guide.what: The Sun and the solar system, how shadows change through the day, and the four directions.
steps: Mark your shadow with chalk in the morning and at noon.
Use a torch and a toy to make shadows.
Find east by watching the sunrise.
home: Make a model of the solar system with fruits of different sizes.
Use a compass app to find north.
guide.watch: The Sun does not really move across the sky; the Earth spins. Explain with a torch and a ball.

title: Allama Iqbal Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 History practice on allama iqbal, from "Life of Iqbal" to "The Falcon". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Recall key facts about Allama Iqbal.
Understand Iqbal's role in the Pakistan Movement.
Understand an idea from Iqbal's poetry.

guide.what: The life and ideas of Allama Muhammad Iqbal, the national poet of Pakistan.
steps: Recite "Lab pe aati hai dua" together.
Find Sialkot and Lahore on a map.
Talk about what being like a shaheen means.
home: Listen to a children's poem by Iqbal.
Visit or look at pictures of Iqbal's tomb.
guide.watch: Iqbal wrote in Urdu and Persian. Children can enjoy his simple poems first.

title: The Pakistan Movement Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 History practice on the pakistan movement, from "Key Events" to "Leaders of the Movement". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know key dates of the Pakistan Movement.
Know leaders of the Pakistan Movement.

guide.what: The main events and leaders of the Pakistan Movement, from 1906 to 1947.
steps: Draw a timeline from 1906 to 1947.
Look at pictures of Minar-e-Pakistan.
Talk about why people wanted a new country.
home: Watch the Pakistan Day parade on TV.
Make a flag and a timeline poster.
guide.watch: History is about people. Focus on leaders' hard work and teamwork, not just dates.

title: Rivers of Pakistan Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Geography practice on rivers of pakistan, from "The Indus River" to "Why Rivers Matter". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know facts about the Indus River.

guide.what: The Indus and the rivers of Punjab, and why rivers matter to Pakistan.
steps: Trace the Indus on a map from north to south.
Talk about dams and why we need them.
Count the five rivers on your fingers.
home: Visit a river or canal bank with the family.
Find out which river is closest to your city.
guide.watch: The Beas mostly flows in India today, but it is still one of Punjab's five rivers.

title: Crops and resources Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Geography practice on crops and resources, from "Crops of Pakistan" to "Uses of Resources". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know major crops and their seasons.
Know where key natural resources are found in Pakistan.

guide.what: Pakistan's main crops, natural resources and how we use them.
steps: Look at food packets and find what they are made from.
Talk about where the gas for the stove comes from.
Find Sui, Khewra and Thar on a map.
home: Visit a farm or a field of wheat.
Buy a piece of pink Khewra salt and look at it.
guide.watch: Rabi crops grow in winter, Kharif crops in summer. Use wheat and rice as the easy examples.

title: Our government Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Social Studies practice on our government, from "What Does Government Do?" to "Taxes". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the federal, provincial and local levels of government.

guide.what: What government does, the levels of government in Pakistan and why taxes matter.
steps: Point out a government service near home: a road, school or hospital.
Explain voting with a family vote on dinner.
Talk about the four provinces.
home: Hold a family election for a weekend activity.
Write a letter to the local council about a problem.
guide.watch: Keep politics out of it. Focus on how government should serve the people.

title: Jobs and professions Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Social Studies practice on jobs and professions, from "Who Makes What?" to "When I Grow Up". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Describe a profession and why it matters.

guide.what: Different professions, goods and services, and respect for all work.
steps: Ask family members about their jobs.
Notice the jobs people do on a street.
Talk about skills each job needs.
home: Interview a relative about their job.
Visit a craftsperson like a potter or tailor.
guide.watch: Avoid ranking jobs. Every job, from sweeper to surgeon, keeps the country running.

title: Cultures of Pakistan Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Social Studies practice on cultures of pakistan, from "Provinces and Languages" to "Unity in Diversity". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the provinces and main languages of Pakistan.
Know foods, crafts and dress from different regions.
Explain what unites people in Pakistan.

guide.what: The many cultures of Pakistan: provinces, languages, food and dress, and what unites us.
steps: Listen to songs in different Pakistani languages.
Cook a dish from another province.
Find each province on a map.
home: Learn to say hello in a new Pakistani language.
Make a scrapbook of cultures.
guide.watch: Many languages are spoken in each province. These are examples, not the only languages.

title: ضمیر کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on pronouns (ضمیر), with an answer key for every page.

guide.what: Pronouns in Urdu: words used instead of names, like میں، تم، وہ.
steps: Retell a story replacing names with pronouns.
Point to people and say میں، تم، وہ.
Explain that آپ shows respect.
home: Talk about family members using pronouns.
Find pronouns in an Urdu storybook.
guide.watch: آپ is used for elders and for respect. Encourage your child to use it with grown-ups.

title: نظم: ہمدردی کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on poem: kindness (نظم: ہمدردی), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read and understand a classic Urdu poem.
Understand the message of a poem.
Learn meanings of words in the poem.

guide.what: Reading Iqbal's poem "Hamdardi" and understanding its message of helping others.
steps: Read the poem aloud and tell the story of the firefly.
Discuss: How can we help someone who is lost or sad?
Explain new words with gestures.
home: Do one kind act each day this week.
Read the full poem and draw the firefly.
guide.watch: The full poem is longer. Read it together over a few days and talk about kindness.

title: درخواست اور خط کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on application and letter (درخواست اور خط), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Complete a leave application in Urdu.
Know the parts of a letter.
Write a short informal letter in Urdu.

guide.what: Writing a leave application and a short letter in Urdu.
steps: Look at a real application and find its parts.
Practise the opening and closing lines.
Talk about polite words: گزارش، شکریہ.
home: Write a real letter to a grandparent and post it.
Write an Eid card in Urdu.
guide.watch: Applications are formal; letters to family are friendly. Compare the two styles.

title: Allah the Creator Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Islamiat practice on allah the creator, from "Allah Is One" to "Saying Thank You". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that Allah is One and the Creator of all.
Use the right words to remember Allah.

guide.what: Allah is One, the Creator of everything, and we thank Him for His blessings.
steps: Name three blessings at dinner each day.
Look at the sky, plants and animals and talk about Allah's creation.
Say Alhamdulillah together after meals.
home: Make a blessings list on the fridge.
Draw a picture of your favourite part of nature.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

title: Wudu and Salah Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Islamiat practice on wudu and salah, from "Steps of Wudu" to "Salah". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the order of the steps of wudu.

guide.what: The steps of wudu and simple facts about Salah.
steps: Practise the steps of wudu together slowly.
Talk about saving water during wudu.
Show which way the Qibla is at home.
home: Make a wudu steps chart for the bathroom.
Go to the mosque together for Jumu'ah if you can.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook. Small differences in the details of wudu are taught by teachers; follow your child's school book.

title: Islamic months Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Islamiat practice on islamic months, from "Months in Order" to "The Moon". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the Islamic months in order.
Know important events in the Islamic year.
Know that Islamic months follow the moon.

guide.what: The twelve Islamic months and the special events in them.
steps: Look at an Islamic calendar together.
Find this month's name in the Islamic calendar.
Look for the new moon at the start of a month.
home: Mark Ramadan and the two Eids on a calendar.
Learn three month names a week.
guide.watch: Islamic months follow the moon, so Ramadan and Eid come about 10 or 11 days earlier each year.

title: Input and output Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Computer practice on input and output, from "Input or Output?" to "Storage". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Input devices send information in, output devices give it out, and storage keeps it.
steps: Type a letter and watch it appear: input then output.
Print a drawing together and talk about output.
Record your voice with the microphone.
home: Make an input and output poster.
Find input and output devices on a phone.
guide.watch: A touchscreen is both input and output. That is a great question for curious children.

title: The desktop Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Computer practice on the desktop, from "Desktop Words" to "Save Your Work". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know parts of the computer desktop.

guide.what: Parts of the desktop, saving work and shutting down a computer correctly.
steps: Show the icons, taskbar and folders on your computer.
Make a folder with your child's name.
Practise saving a drawing.
home: Make a desktop picture on paper with icons.
Practise shutting down properly.
guide.watch: Different computers look a little different. Teach the idea, not one exact screen.

words: a small picture for a program
a box where a program opens

title: Staying safe online Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Computer practice on staying safe online, from "Safe or Not Safe?" to "If Something Feels Wrong". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what information to keep private.
Know what to do if something online feels wrong.

guide.what: Keeping personal information private and asking a grown-up for help online.
steps: Agree on family internet rules.
Use devices in a shared room.
Tell your child they will never be in trouble for telling you.
home: Make a family online rules poster.
Practise saying "I will ask a grown-up first".
guide.watch: Children should feel safe telling you anything. Stay calm when they share something worrying.

title: The Holy Quran Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Islamiat practice on the holy quran, from "Quran Facts" to "Holy Books". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know basic facts about the Holy Quran.
Show respect for the Holy Quran.
Know the holy books revealed by Allah.

guide.what: Basic facts about the Holy Quran, respecting it, and the holy books revealed by Allah.
steps: Show your child where the Quran is kept at home and why.
Count the paras and surahs together in a mushaf.
Talk about how the Quran was revealed.
home: Listen to a short surah together each day.
Read the Quran with a qualified teacher.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

title: Prophets of Allah Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Islamiat practice on prophets of allah, from "First and Last" to "What Prophets Taught". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the first and last prophets.
Know a famous event from the life of some prophets.

guide.what: Prophets of Allah, the first and last prophets, and famous events from their lives.
steps: Read a prophet story from a children's Islamiat book.
Talk about what each prophet teaches us.
Say (AS) and (PBUH) after their names.
home: Make a prophets timeline from Hazrat Adam (AS) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
Draw the ark of Hazrat Nuh (AS).
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

title: Life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Islamiat practice on life of the holy prophet (pbuh), from "Early Life" to "His Good Qualities". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know facts about the early life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
Know about the Hijrah to Madinah.
Learn the good qualities of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

guide.what: The early life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), the Hijrah and his good qualities.
steps: Read a seerah story from your child's Islamiat book.
Pick one good quality and practise it for a week.
Find Makkah and Madinah on a map.
home: Make a good qualities chart and tick it daily.
Ask your child to retell one seerah story.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

title: Hardware and software Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Computer practice on hardware and software, from "Hardware or Software?" to "Computer Jobs". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Choose the right software for a job.

guide.what: Hardware is what we can touch; software is the set of instructions that makes it work.
steps: Point to hardware and open software on your computer.
Talk about which app you use for which job.
Explain that apps on a phone are software too.
home: Make a hardware and software sorting game.
Try a new learning app together.
guide.watch: The operating system is the big program that runs all the others. Use a phone as an example.

title: Typing and documents Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Computer practice on typing and documents, from "Word Processor Words" to "Home Row". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the home row for typing.

guide.what: Word processing, formatting and keyboard shortcuts, and the home row keys for typing.
steps: Type a short paragraph and make one word bold.
Find the bumps on F and J.
Practise one shortcut each day.
home: Type a birthday card for a relative.
Use a free typing game for 10 minutes.
guide.watch: Correct finger placement now saves bad habits later. Short practice is best.

title: The internet Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Computer practice on the internet, from "Internet Words" to "Being Kind Online". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Using the internet: browsers, search engines, strong passwords and being kind online.
steps: Search for a school topic together and compare two sites.
Make a strong password together using a fun phrase.
Talk about kind and unkind messages.
home: Write family rules for messaging apps.
Find an answer online and check it in a book.
guide.watch: Children believe what they read online. Teach them to ask "Who wrote this and how do they know?"

title: Kalima and Bismillah Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Islamiat practice on kalima and bismillah, from "Kalima Tayyiba" to "Allah's Gifts". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Recite the Kalima Tayyiba and know its meaning.
Know Bismillah, its meaning and when we say it.
Know that Allah is the Creator of everything.

guide.what: The Kalima Tayyiba and Bismillah, their meanings, and Allah as the Creator.
steps: Say Bismillah together before meals.
Recite the Kalima slowly, one part at a time.
Look at nature and talk about Allah's creation.
home: Make Bismillah a family habit before eating and starting homework.
Go for a walk and name things Allah created.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

title: Pillars of Islam Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Islamiat practice on pillars of islam, from "Five Pillars" to "Ramadan". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the five pillars of Islam.
Name the five daily prayers and their times.
Know simple facts about fasting in Ramadan.

guide.what: The five pillars of Islam and the five daily prayers.
steps: Count the five pillars on one hand.
Point to the sky at each prayer time and name it.
Talk about what your family does in Ramadan.
home: Make a five pillars hand print poster.
Listen for the azan and name the prayer.
guide.watch: Sehri is the meal before dawn and Iftar is the meal at sunset. Children often mix them up.

title: Good manners Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Islamiat practice on good manners, from "Greetings" to "My Good Deed". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use Islamic greetings and good words.

guide.what: Islamic greetings and good manners at home, school and with others.
steps: Greet family members with Assalam o Alaikum every morning.
Praise your child when they use good words.
Talk about kindness to neighbours.
home: Keep a good deeds jar: add a bead for each kind act.
Practise saying JazakAllah when someone helps.
guide.watch: Children learn manners by watching. Use these words yourself every day.

title: Parts of a computer Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Computer practice on parts of a computer, from "Name the Parts" to "Computer Words". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the main parts of a computer.

guide.what: The main parts of a computer and computers we see around us.
steps: Point to each part of a computer or laptop and name it.
Talk about devices at home that have a computer inside.
Let your child press the power button with you.
home: Draw and label a computer.
Look for screens and buttons on machines when you go out.
guide.watch: A laptop has the same parts as a desktop, just joined together. Point them out.

title: Mouse and keyboard Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Computer practice on mouse and keyboard, from "Mouse Actions" to "Sit Right". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know special keys on the keyboard.
Use a computer safely and comfortably.

guide.what: Using the mouse and keyboard, and sitting correctly at a computer.
steps: Let your child practise clicking and dragging in a drawing app.
Show the space bar, enter and backspace keys.
Set a timer for short screen sessions.
home: Type your child's name together.
Play a simple mouse game together.
guide.watch: Small hands may find a big mouse hard. A touchpad or small mouse helps.

words: move up and down the page

title: Using computers Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Computer practice on using computers, from "What Can We Do?" to "Draw a Computer". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: What we can do with computers and healthy screen habits.
steps: Show your child two things you use a computer for at work or home.
Agree on simple screen time rules.
Praise your child for asking before using a device.
home: Use a paint program together.
Make a screen time chart.
guide.watch: Screens are useful, but play, books and sleep come first at this age.

title: Measuring Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on measuring, from "Longer or Shorter?" to "Holds More". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Comparing length, weight and how much things hold, and measuring with hands and feet.
steps: Measure a table with hand spans together.
Compare two cups by pouring water.
Use words: longer, shorter, heavier, lighter, holds more.
home: Measure your room in footsteps.
Weigh fruit with your hands before using a scale.
guide.watch: Hand spans differ from person to person. That is why we need rulers later.

title: Plants around us Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on plants around us, from "Parts of a Plant" to "Grow a Seed". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what plants need to grow.

guide.what: Parts of a plant and what plants need to grow.
steps: Look at a plant and name its parts.
Plant a seed in a cup and water it.
Talk about plants we eat.
home: Grow mint or coriander on a window sill.
Collect leaves of different shapes.
guide.watch: Plants need light to make food. Try one seed in the dark to see the difference.

title: Road safety Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on road safety, from "Traffic Lights" to "Stop, Look, Listen". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Staying safe on the road: traffic lights, zebra crossings and seatbelts.
steps: Practise stop, look, listen on every walk.
Point out traffic lights and zebra crossings.
Always wear seatbelts in the car.
home: Make paper traffic lights and play "red light, green light".
Talk about safe places to play.
guide.watch: Children can't judge speed well. They must always cross with a grown-up.

title: Action words Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Nursery English practice on action words, from "Do the Action" to "Draw an Action". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Hear and act out action words.

guide.what: Action words tell us what someone is doing: run, jump, clap, eat.
steps: Play "Simon says" with action words.
Say what you are doing while you do it: I am cooking.
Act out an action and let your child guess.
home: Play musical statues and name the action before each freeze.
Look at people in the park and say what they are doing.
guide.watch: Children often understand actions before they can say them. Keep acting and naming together.

title: Sounds c, m, d, g Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Nursery English practice on sounds c, m, d, g, from "Trace c m d g" to "Sound Hunt". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Trace the letters c, m, d and g and say their sounds.
Hear the first sound of a word.
Find things that start with a sound.

guide.what: The sounds c, m, d and g and hearing them at the start of words.
steps: Say the sound clearly: "mmm" like something yummy.
Show a real object with that first sound.
Trace the letter in the air while saying the sound.
home: Sort toys by their first sound.
Play I Spy with these four sounds.
guide.watch: d and g can be tricky to write. Trace d as "c then a tall line".

title: One more, one less Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on one more, one less, from "One More" to "Count the Stars". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Find one more than a number to 10.
Find one less than a number to 10.

guide.what: Finding one more and one less than a number.
steps: Use real things: 3 spoons, add one more. How many?
Take one away and count again.
Say "one more" and "one less" in daily life.
home: Count stairs up (one more) and down (one less).
Play with blocks: build a tower one block taller.
guide.watch: Children may count everything again. Show that one more is just the next number.

title: Simple patterns Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on simple patterns, from "What Comes Next?" to "Make a Pattern". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Patterns repeat in the same order again and again.
steps: Clap a pattern: clap, stamp, clap, stamp.
Make patterns with buttons or pasta.
Say the pattern out loud before adding the next piece.
home: Thread beads in a two-colour pattern.
Find patterns on clothes and tiles.
guide.watch: Start with two items (AB). Move to ABC only when AB is easy.

title: First, next, last Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on first, next, last, from "Who Is First?" to "Draw the Line". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Using first, second, next and last to talk about order.
steps: Line up toys and ask who is first and last.
Talk through your routine: first, next, last.
Have a family race and name the places.
home: Line up for the bathroom: who is first?
Retell a story using first, next and last.
guide.watch: First and last are easier than second and third. Start there.

title: Counting back and zero Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on counting back and zero, from "Rocket Countdown" to "Count and Colour". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Counting back from 10 and knowing that zero means none.
steps: Count down like a rocket: 10, 9, 8... blast off!
Show an empty plate: zero rotis.
Count back while walking down the stairs.
home: Play hide the toys: how many are left?
Sing a counting-down song.
guide.watch: Zero is tricky. Use "nothing left" and an empty bowl to show it.

title: Weather Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on weather, from "What Is the Weather?" to "Today's Weather". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Kinds of weather and what to wear.
steps: Look out of the window each morning and name the weather.
Feel the wind and the sun together.
Talk about what to wear today.
home: Make a weather chart with pictures for a week.
Jump in puddles after the rain.
guide.watch: Young children love routine. A weather chat every morning builds vocabulary.

title: Day and night Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on day and night, from "Day or Night?" to "My Bedtime". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: What we see and do in the day and at night.
steps: Look at the sky in the day and at night together.
Talk about which animals sleep in the day, like owls.
Keep a calm bedtime routine.
home: Read a bedtime story every night.
Spot the moon from the window.
guide.watch: The moon can sometimes be seen in the day. That is a great question to talk about.

title: Clothes Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on clothes, from "Name the Clothes" to "Dress Up". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Names of clothes and what to wear in hot and cold weather.
steps: Name each piece of clothing as your child dresses.
Let your child choose clothes for the weather.
Practise buttons and zips.
home: Sort laundry into summer and winter clothes.
Play dress-up.
guide.watch: Let your child try dressing alone, even if it takes longer.

title: Good manners Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on good manners, from "Magic Words" to "My Kind Act". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use please, thank you and sorry.
Tell kind actions from unkind ones.

guide.what: Polite words and kind actions with family and friends.
steps: Model please, thank you and sorry yourself.
Praise kind acts straight away.
Role play sharing with toys.
home: Make a kindness jar and add a bead for each kind act.
Help a neighbour together.
guide.watch: Saying sorry takes practice. Show how to say it and then fix the problem.

title: جسم کے حصے کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on parts of the body (جسم کے حصے), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Name parts of the body in Urdu.
Count body parts and write the number.

guide.what: Naming parts of the body in Urdu.
steps: Touch and name body parts in Urdu.
Sing a body parts song in Urdu.
Ask: آنکھ سے ہم کیا کرتے ہیں؟
home: Play "touch your ناک".
Count fingers in Urdu.
guide.watch: Mixing English and Urdu body words is common. Repeat the Urdu word gently.

title: پھل اور سبزیاں کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on fruits and vegetables (پھل اور سبزیاں), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Sort fruits and vegetables in Urdu.

guide.what: Names of fruits and vegetables in Urdu.
steps: Name fruits in Urdu at the market.
Let your child pick a fruit and name it.
Sort fruits and vegetables at home.
home: Make a fruit chaat and name each fruit in Urdu.
Draw your favourite fruit.
guide.watch: Some fruits have English names used in Urdu (like کیوی). That is fine.

title: جانوروں کے نام کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on animal names (جانوروں کے نام), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Name animals and their sounds in Urdu.

guide.what: Animal names and sounds in Urdu.
steps: Make animal sounds together and name them in Urdu.
Visit a park or zoo and name the animals.
Read an Urdu animal book.
home: Play "which animal says..."
Draw a farm with animals.
guide.watch: Young children love animal sounds. Use them to learn new words.

title: گنتی ۶ سے ۱۰ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on counting 6 to 10 (گنتی ۶ سے ۱۰), with an answer key for every page.

guide.what: Counting and writing numbers six to ten in Urdu.
steps: Count steps in Urdu.
Write Urdu numbers on cards and put them in order.
Count rotis at dinner in Urdu.
home: Play hopscotch with Urdu numbers.
Count fingers on both hands in Urdu.
guide.watch: Urdu digits look different from English digits. Show both side by side.

title: Capital and small letters Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of KG English practice on capital and small letters, from "Match the Letters" to "Capital or Small?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell capital and small letters apart.

guide.what: Every letter has a capital and a small shape. Names start with a capital letter.
steps: Show the two shapes side by side and trace both.
Write your child's name and point to the capital.
Spot capitals on signs and packets.
home: Match magnetic or paper letters into pairs.
Find capital letters in a newspaper headline.
guide.watch: Some pairs look very different (G and g, R and r). Practise those more.

title: Naming and doing words Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of KG English practice on naming and doing words, from "Naming Words" to "Naming or Doing?". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Naming words name things (cat, bus). Doing words tell an action (run, sing).
steps: Point to things and say: that is a naming word.
Do an action and say: this is a doing word.
Make two-word sentences: Dogs bark.
home: Play naming and doing word charades.
Make silly sentences with one of each.
guide.watch: At this age the names matter less than the idea. "Thing words" and "action words" are fine too.

title: Ordinal numbers Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on ordinal numbers, from "1st to 5th" to "Days in Order". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use ordinal numbers in a story.

guide.what: Ordinal numbers tell position: first, second, third.
steps: Line up toys and name each place.
Talk about who was first to wake up.
Use 1st, 2nd, 3rd with dates.
home: Hold a family race and give places.
Find 1st, 2nd and 3rd on the calendar.
guide.watch: Children confuse "two" and "second". Say both: number two is in second place.

title: Counting in 2s, 5s and 10s Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on counting in 2s, 5s and 10s, from "Count in 2s" to "Count in 5s". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Counting in groups of two, five and ten.
steps: Count shoes in pairs: 2, 4, 6.
Count fingers on hands in fives.
Count ten-rupee notes in tens.
home: Skip and count in twos.
Count toes of the whole family in fives.
guide.watch: Counting in tens is easiest. Start there if twos are hard.

title: Coins and notes Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on coins and notes, from "Know the Coins" to "Add the Coins". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Naming Pakistani coins and adding small amounts.
steps: Let your child hold and sort real coins.
Play shop with toy prices under Rs 10.
Count coins into a piggy bank.
home: Let your child pay for a small item with your help.
Sort coins by value.
guide.watch: A bigger coin is not always worth more. Look at the number.

title: Time words Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on time words, from "Morning, Afternoon, Night" to "O'Clock". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Order the days of the week.
Read the time to the hour.

guide.what: Words for time: morning, afternoon, night, days of the week and o'clock.
steps: Talk about what you do in the morning and at night.
Sing the days of the week.
Show o'clock on a real clock.
home: Ask: What day is it today?
Make a paper plate clock.
guide.watch: Yesterday and tomorrow are hard words. Use them often in daily talk.

title: My five senses Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on my five senses, from "Which Sense?" to "Loud or Soft?". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Our five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.
steps: Do a blindfold smell test with safe kitchen things.
Listen with eyes closed and name the sounds.
Touch things and say rough, smooth, soft or hard.
home: Go on a senses walk in the park.
Taste sweet, sour and salty foods.
guide.watch: Never taste unknown things. Explain that some senses need grown-up help.

title: Water Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on water, from "Uses of Water" to "Save Water". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Where water comes from, how we use it and why we save it.
steps: Count the ways your family uses water today.
Turn off the tap while brushing teeth.
Water plants together.
home: Collect rainwater for plants.
Make a "save water" sticker.
guide.watch: Pakistan needs to save water. Small habits at home make a big difference.

title: Festivals Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on festivals, from "Which Festival?" to "My Festival". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Festivals we celebrate in Pakistan and how we celebrate them.
steps: Look at photos from last Eid and talk about them.
Make a card for a relative.
Talk about how friends of other faiths celebrate.
home: Help prepare a festival dish.
Decorate with flags for 14 August.
guide.watch: Festivals are about sharing and family. Talk about giving as well as getting.

title: Birds and insects Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on birds and insects, from "Bird or Insect?" to "Where Do They Live?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know birds have 2 legs and insects have 6.
Know homes of birds and insects.

guide.what: Birds and insects around us, their legs and their homes.
steps: Watch birds and insects in the garden.
Count legs on a picture of an insect.
Talk about how bees help flowers.
home: Put out water for birds in summer.
Draw a butterfly.
guide.watch: Spiders are not insects; they have 8 legs. A fun fact for curious children.

title: آسان واحد جمع کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on one and many (آسان واحد جمع), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Tell one from many in Urdu.

guide.what: Simple singular and plural words in Urdu.
steps: Show one thing and many things and say both words.
Count toys and say the plural.
Point out word endings that change.
home: Play "one or many" with fruit.
Count birds outside in Urdu.
guide.watch: Some words do not change. Learn the common ones first.

title: آسان متضاد کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on easy opposites (آسان متضاد), with an answer key for every page.

guide.what: Easy opposite words in Urdu.
steps: Act out opposites: اوپر، نیچے.
Show a big and a small spoon.
Say a word and let your child say the opposite.
home: Play opposites with toys.
Find hot and cold things in the kitchen.
guide.watch: Opposites help vocabulary grow fast. Practise a few each day.

title: دنوں کے نام کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on days of the week (دنوں کے نام), with an answer key for every page.

guide.what: The seven days of the week in Urdu.
steps: Say the day in Urdu every morning.
Sing the days in order.
Match each day to an activity.
home: Make a weekly chart with Urdu day names.
Ask: کل کون سا دن تھا؟
guide.watch: Many families say days in English. Using the Urdu names daily helps them stick.

title: آسان مذکر مؤنث کی مشق
en: Boy words and girl words practice
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on boy words and girl words (آسان مذکر مؤنث), with an answer key for every page.

guide.what: Simple masculine and feminine words in Urdu.
steps: Name family members in pairs: دادا، دادی.
Play animal pairs: شیر، شیرنی.
Notice that ا often becomes ی.
home: Make family pair cards.
Talk about relatives using Urdu words.
guide.watch: Some pairs are different words (ابو، امی). Learn them as pairs.

title: Shapes and symmetry Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on shapes and symmetry, from "Faces, Edges, Corners" to "Draw the Other Half". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Describing 3D shapes and finding lines of symmetry.
steps: Fold paper in half and cut a shape to see symmetry.
Count faces of a box together.
Look for symmetry in leaves and faces.
home: Make ink blot butterflies.
Find symmetric patterns on tiles and rugs.
guide.watch: Some shapes have more than one line of symmetry. A square has four!

title: Halves and quarters Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on halves and quarters, from "Halves and Quarters" to "Quarters". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Halves and quarters are equal parts of a whole.
steps: Cut a roti into two equal halves.
Fold paper into quarters.
Share sweets into two equal groups.
home: Cut fruit into halves and quarters at snack time.
Fold a napkin into quarters.
guide.watch: Halves must be equal. A big piece and a small piece are not halves.

title: Pictographs Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on pictographs, from "Read the Pictograph" to "Make a Pictograph". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Collect data and make a pictograph.

guide.what: Collecting information and showing it with tally marks and pictographs.
steps: Ask family members a question and record answers with tally marks.
Read a pictograph together and ask how many.
Compare: which has most, which has fewest?
home: Count cars by colour on a walk.
Make a chart of favourite foods.
guide.watch: Tally marks are grouped in fives. Show how the fifth line crosses the four.

title: Sharing and division Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on sharing and division, from "Share Equally" to "Division Facts". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Division means sharing equally or making equal groups.
steps: Share real things between plates.
Count how many groups of 2 you can make.
Link division to times tables: 5 × 2 = 10, so 10 ÷ 2 = 5.
home: Share snacks equally between siblings.
Pack eggs into groups.
guide.watch: Make sure shares are equal. Ask: Is it fair?

title: Materials Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on materials, from "Natural or Man-made?" to "Right Material". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Materials have different properties, so we use them for different jobs.
steps: Collect objects and describe how they feel.
Test which things let light through.
Talk about why a spoon is metal.
home: Sort kitchen things by material.
Test which materials soak up water.
guide.watch: Paper is made from wood, so some say it is natural. Explain it is changed by people.

title: Push and pull Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on push and pull, from "Push or Pull?" to "Rough or Smooth". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know forces can change speed, direction and shape.

guide.what: Pushes and pulls are forces that make things move, stop or change shape.
steps: Push and pull toys and name the force.
Roll a toy car on different floors.
Squash playdough and talk about shape changes.
home: Play tug of war.
Make a ramp with a book and roll toys down.
guide.watch: Friction slows things down. Rough surfaces have more friction.

title: Light and shadows Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on light and shadows, from "Light Sources" to "Shadow Fun". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Light comes from sources, and shadows form when something blocks light.
steps: Make shadow puppets with a torch.
Look at shadows in the morning and at noon.
Talk about why the Moon shines.
home: Trace your shadow with chalk.
Play shadow tag outside.
guide.watch: The Moon is not a light source; it reflects the Sun's light.

title: What animals eat Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on what animals eat, from "Plant or Meat Eaters" to "Teeth Tell". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Animals eat plants, meat or both, and food chains show who eats what.
steps: Talk about what pets eat.
Draw a food chain starting with a plant.
Look at pictures of animal teeth.
home: Visit a zoo or farm and ask what each animal eats.
Make a food chain paper strip.
guide.watch: Every food chain starts with a plant, because plants make food from sunlight.

title: Ancient Greece Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 History practice on ancient greece, from "Greek Facts" to "My Olympic Event". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Ancient Greece gave us the Olympic Games, theatre and the idea of voting.
steps: Look at pictures of Greek temples.
Talk about the Olympics today.
Hold a family vote on a game.
home: Hold mini Olympics at home.
Make a paper column.
guide.watch: Keep it simple: what they built, what they played and what they believed in.

title: The Mughals Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 History practice on the mughals, from "Mughal Buildings" to "Design a Garden". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: The Mughal emperors and the buildings and gardens they left in Pakistan.
steps: Look at photos of Badshahi Mosque and Lahore Fort.
Find Lahore and Thatta on a map.
Talk about why gardens were important.
home: Visit a Mughal site if you can.
Draw a pattern like Mughal tiles.
guide.watch: Mughal history is long. Focus on the buildings children can visit today.

title: Inventions Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 History practice on inventions, from "Old and New" to "Invent Something". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Inventions changed how people live, from the wheel to the mobile phone.
steps: Talk about things that did not exist when grandparents were young.
Look at an old object and guess how it worked.
Discuss what you would invent.
home: Make a simple invention from recycled materials.
Interview grandparents about technology.
guide.watch: Every invention solves a problem. Ask: What problem did this solve?

title: Pakistani heroes Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 History practice on pakistani heroes, from "Who Is It?" to "My Hero". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Pakistanis who did great things for others and for the country.
steps: Read about one hero each day.
Talk about the qualities heroes share.
Talk about everyday heroes like teachers and nurses.
home: Make a hero poster.
Thank an everyday hero in your area.
guide.watch: Heroes are not only famous people. Grandparents and teachers can be heroes too.

title: Old places Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 History practice on old places, from "Famous Old Places" to "Time Capsule". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Historic places and museums in Pakistan, and why we protect them.
steps: Visit a museum or historic place.
Look at old coins or photos at home.
Talk about why we must not write on old walls.
home: Make a family time capsule.
Take a virtual museum tour online.
guide.watch: Teach respect for old buildings: no writing or scratching on them.

title: Land and water Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on land and water, from "Land or Water?" to "In Pakistan". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Different landforms and bodies of water, with examples from Pakistan.
steps: Look at photos of mountains, deserts and seas.
Make landforms with playdough.
Find K2 and the Indus on a map.
home: Build a sand model of a mountain and valley.
Visit a lake or river.
guide.watch: Islands are a fun idea. Use a stone in a bowl of water to show one.

title: Globes and maps Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on globes and maps, from "Globe Words" to "Hot or Cold?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know places near the poles and equator are different.

guide.what: Using a globe and reading symbols on maps.
steps: Spin a globe and find Pakistan.
Point to the poles and the equator.
Draw a map key together.
home: Make a map of your room with a key.
Find Pakistan on a world map.
guide.watch: A globe is a model of the Earth; a map is flat. Compare them side by side.

title: My neighbourhood map Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on my neighbourhood map, from "Places Nearby" to "Draw My Area". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use left, right, forward and back.

guide.what: Places in the neighbourhood and giving directions.
steps: Walk around the block and name the places.
Practise left and right on walks.
Draw a simple map together.
home: Give directions to find a hidden toy.
Draw your route to school.
guide.watch: Left and right take time. A band on one wrist can help.

title: Countries and flags Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on countries and flags, from "Neighbours" to "Our Flag". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Pakistan's neighbours, some capital cities and flags.
steps: Find each country on a world map.
Look at flags and talk about their colours.
Talk about relatives who live in other countries.
home: Make a flag collection.
Try a dish from a neighbouring country.
guide.watch: Children enjoy flags. Use them to learn country names.

title: Natural wonders Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on natural wonders, from "Wonders of Pakistan" to "Postcard". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Natural wonders of Pakistan: mountains, plateaus, lakes and parks.
steps: Look at photos of northern Pakistan together.
Find each place on a map.
Talk about protecting nature.
home: Plan a dream family trip in Pakistan.
Make a postcard to send to a friend.
guide.watch: Pakistan has many of the world's highest mountains. A great point of pride.

title: Needs and wants Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on needs and wants, from "Need or Want?" to "Saving Money". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the basic needs of people.

guide.what: Needs are things we must have; wants are things we would like.
steps: Sort a shopping list into needs and wants.
Talk about why we cannot buy every want.
Start a small savings jar.
home: Plan a pretend budget for a week.
Give extra clothes to someone in need.
guide.watch: Wants are not bad. Teach that we take care of needs first.

title: Transport Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on transport, from "Land, Water, Air" to "Pakistani Transport". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Compare transport in the past and today.

guide.what: Ways of travelling on land, water and in the air, then and now.
steps: Name the vehicles you see on a drive.
Talk about how grandparents travelled.
Look at a map and plan a train trip.
home: Ride a public bus or train with your child.
Make a transport collage.
guide.watch: Talk about safe and clean transport, like walking and buses.

title: Communication Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on communication, from "Ways to Talk" to "Write a Message". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Compare communication in the past and today.

guide.what: The many ways people share messages, in the past and today.
steps: Write and post a real letter to a relative.
Talk about how messages travelled long ago.
Learn a few signs in sign language.
home: Make paper cup telephones.
Video call a grandparent and tell them about school.
guide.watch: Teach kind and safe messaging early, even before children have phones.

words: talk with your voice far away
a message sent on a computer

title: A clean environment Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on a clean environment, from "Clean or Dirty?" to "Clean-up Plan". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Choose ways to keep the environment clean.

guide.what: Keeping our homes, streets and country clean, and kinds of pollution.
steps: Pick up litter together in the park.
Carry a bag for wrappers on trips.
Talk about why smog happens in winter.
home: Plant a tree with your child.
Sort rubbish at home.
guide.watch: Lead by example. Children copy what they see adults do with rubbish.

title: Rules and laws Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on rules and laws, from "Why Rules?" to "Class Rules". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Rules and laws keep us safe and help everyone be treated fairly.
steps: Make family rules together.
Talk about what happens if no one follows rules.
Notice signs with rules in public places.
home: Play a game, then break a rule on purpose and talk about fairness.
Find rule signs in a park.
guide.watch: Explain the reason behind each rule. Children follow rules they understand.

title: Helping others Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on helping others, from "Ways to Help" to "My Helping Plan". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Learn about a Pakistani who helped others.

guide.what: Helping people in need, and learning from people like Abdul Sattar Edhi.
steps: Talk about someone who helped your family.
Do a kind act together this week.
Read about the Edhi Foundation.
home: Give toys you no longer use to children in need.
Help an elderly neighbour.
guide.watch: Helping does not need money. Time and kindness count too.

title: Goods and services Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on goods and services, from "Goods or Services?" to "Buyers and Sellers". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know shops and what they sell.

guide.what: Goods are things we buy; services are jobs people do for us.
steps: Visit a bazaar and name the goods and services.
Let your child pay at a shop.
Talk about jobs that give services.
home: Play shop at home with price tags.
Make a list of services your family uses.
guide.watch: Every job is valuable, whether it makes goods or gives a service.

title: ہم آواز الفاظ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on rhyming words (ہم آواز الفاظ), with an answer key for every page.

guide.what: Words that sound alike at the end, and making simple rhymes.
steps: Say pairs of rhyming words aloud.
Clap when you hear a rhyme in a poem.
Make silly rhymes together.
home: Read an Urdu poem and find rhyming words.
Play a rhyming game in the car.
guide.watch: Rhymes in Urdu often end with the same sound and letter. Listen to the endings.

title: حروفِ تہجی کی ترتیب کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on alphabetical order (حروفِ تہجی کی ترتیب), with an answer key for every page.

guide.what: Putting words in alphabetical order and using a dictionary.
steps: Say the Urdu alphabet together.
Sort word cards by first letter.
Look up a word in an Urdu dictionary.
home: Make a mini picture dictionary.
Order family names alphabetically.
guide.watch: Children need the alphabet order secure before using a dictionary. Revise it first.

title: دعوت نامہ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on invitation (دعوت نامہ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Know the parts of an invitation.

guide.what: Writing an invitation in Urdu with who, why, when and where.
steps: Look at a real wedding or party card.
Find who, what, when and where on it.
Write an invitation for a family event.
home: Make an invitation for a tea party with toys.
Write an Eid dinner invitation.
guide.watch: Invitations must have the day, time and place. Use a checklist.

title: کہانی: لالچی کتا کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on story: the greedy dog (کہانی: لالچی کتا), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read a story and answer questions.
Find the moral of a story.

guide.what: Reading a classic Urdu story and finding its lesson.
steps: Read the story aloud with expression.
Ask: Why did the dog lose the bone?
Talk about being happy with what we have.
home: Act out the story with a toy dog.
Draw the dog on the bridge.
guide.watch: Many Urdu stories end with a lesson (سبق). Ask your child to say it in their own words.

title: Angels Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Islamiat practice on angels, from "Four Angels" to "Good Deeds". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the duties of four well-known angels.
Remember that good deeds are recorded.

guide.what: Angels are created by Allah and always obey Him; believing in them is part of faith.
steps: Read about angels in your child's Islamiat book.
Talk about doing good deeds every day.
Keep the discussion calm and simple.
home: Keep a good deeds diary.
Draw a picture of something good you did.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

title: The Holy Prophet's childhood Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Islamiat practice on the holy prophet's childhood, from "Early Years" to "Like the Holy Prophet (PBUH)". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know facts about the Holy Prophet's (PBUH) childhood.

Find loops in songs and games.
Try a block coding game with loops.

Use a free block coding app together.
guide.watch: Loops are everywhere: in songs, games and exercise routines.

guide.what: Finding and fixing mistakes in instructions and code.
steps: Mix up a routine's steps and ask your child to fix them.
Praise careful checking.
Talk about how mistakes help us learn.
home: Find the mistakes in silly instructions.
Try a puzzle coding game.
guide.watch: Bugs are normal. Even expert programmers spend lots of time debugging.

guide.what: Being kind online and knowing what to do about unkind messages.

Make a plan for what to do if someone is unkind.
Praise kind messages.
home: Write kind messages to family members.
Role play telling a grown-up.
guide.watch: Children should never handle online bullying alone. Keep communication open.

obj: Decide what is safe to post.

steps: Talk about what is OK to share online.
Ask: Would I be happy for everyone to see this?
Check privacy settings together.
home: Make a "think before you post" poster.
Look at what is online about your family together.
guide.watch: Even deleted posts can be saved by others. Teach caution early.

steps: Look at robots in videos.
Talk about jobs robots can and cannot do.
Discuss checking answers from smart assistants.

Watch a Mars rover video.
guide.watch: Remind children that smart machines can make mistakes. People should always check.

Talk about one blessing each day.
Learn one name and its meaning a week.

Draw a thank-you picture.

steps: Make hand washing a habit before meals.
Tidy toys together every evening.
Talk about why cleanliness keeps us healthy.
home: Make a cleanliness chart with stickers.
Clean a corner of the garden together.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

steps: Give your child a small daily job.
Model respectful speech with grandparents.
Praise respectful behaviour.
home: Make a surprise card for parents or grandparents.
Serve tea to elders.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

guide.what: Telling the truth and being honest, even when it is hard.
steps: Praise honesty, even when your child admits a mistake.
Talk about the Holy Prophet (PBUH) being called As-Sadiq, the truthful.
Read a story about honesty.
home: Keep a truth jar: add a bead for honest choices.
Role play honest choices.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

Practise quiet voices for the mosque.
Listen to the azan and talk about it.
home: Draw famous mosques like Faisal Mosque and Badshahi Mosque.
Go for Jumu'ah prayer together.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

guide.what: Ramadan, fasting, good deeds and the joy of Eid-ul-Fitr.
steps: Talk about why we fast and share.
Let your child help prepare iftar.
Make Eid cards together.
home: Make a Ramadan good deeds calendar.
Give food to someone in need.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

title: Kindness to animals Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Islamiat practice on kindness to animals, from "Kind or Unkind?" to "Bird Water Pot". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Islam teaches kindness to animals and care for plants.
steps: Put water out for birds on hot days.
Talk about being gentle with pets.
Plant a tree together.
home: Make a bird feeder.
Water the plants every day.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

Explain why we save work first.
Show the power button.
home: Let your child switch on the computer with you.
Make a step card for the computer desk.
guide.watch: Children often press buttons many times. Teach them to wait patiently.

title: Drawing on the computer Practice

guide.what: Using a paint program to draw and colour pictures.
steps: Open a paint program together.
Try each tool and talk about it.
Save the picture with your child's name.
home: Draw a house using shapes.
Print a favourite computer drawing.
guide.watch: Drawing with a mouse is hard for small hands. A touchscreen can help.

title: Letters on the keyboard Practice

guide.what: Finding letters on the keyboard and typing your name.
steps: Let your child find each letter of their name.
Show the shift key for capitals.
Type short words together.
home: Play a letter hunt on the keyboard.
Type a short message to a relative.
guide.watch: Keyboard letters are in capitals, but they type small letters. Explain this.

obj: Know why we care for computers.

guide.what: Looking after computers and using them carefully.
steps: Keep food and drinks away from devices.
Wash hands before using the computer.
Show gentle typing.
home: Make a computer rules sign.
Clean the screen together with a soft cloth.
guide.watch: Devices are expensive. Simple care rules protect them.

title: Devices around us Practice

guide.what: Digital devices we see and use every day.
steps: Name the devices in your home.
Talk about what each one is for.
Agree on device rules.
home: Make a device scrapbook.
Count the screens at home.
guide.watch: Talk about using devices for learning as well as fun.

title: Instructions in order Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Computer practice on instructions in order, from "Right Order" to "Give Instructions". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Computers follow instructions in order. This is the first step in coding.
steps: Play "robot": give your child step-by-step moves.
Mix up the steps of a routine and fix them.
Explain that computers do exactly what we tell them.
home: Write instructions for making tea, then follow them exactly.
Draw a path for a toy robot.
guide.watch: Computers cannot guess. Show how a missing step makes things go wrong.

title: Safe internet Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Computer practice on safe internet, from "Ask First" to "Safe Rules". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Using the internet only with a grown-up and keeping private things private.
steps: Sit with your child when they are online.
Agree on safe websites and apps.
Tell your child they can always come to you.
home: Make a family internet rules poster.
Practise saying "I will ask first".
guide.watch: Young children should only go online with an adult nearby.

title: Maths Revision Set
subject: Maths

guide.what: Your child counts objects to 20, reads and writes the numbers, and learns that 11 to 19 are one ten and some ones.
steps: Count real things, touching each one as you say the number.
Write 1 to 20 on a strip of paper. Point as you count forwards, then backwards.
Show 14 as a bundle of 10 sticks and 4 loose sticks: one ten and four ones.
home: Count rotis, stairs or cars on the road.
Ask: What comes after 13? What comes before 20?
guide.watch: Teen numbers are often written backwards, like 41 for 14. Say "ten comes first" and write the 1 first.

obj: Revise every topic from the term before a test.

steps: Ask: What makes the fan move? What lets you run and play?
Sort things that need electricity from things that do not.
Talk about food as fuel for the body.
home: Spot everything that uses electricity in one room.
Go on a switch-off patrol for lights nobody is using.
guide.watch: Keep it concrete. Your child does not need a deep explanation of electricity yet.

steps: Look at family photos and name each person.
Say English and Urdu words together: grandmother, Dadi or Nani.
Talk about the jobs each person does at home.
home: Draw a family tree together.
Give one small helping job each day.
guide.watch: Families look different. Make sure every kind of family feels normal to your child.

Trace the line in the air with a finger first, then on paper.
Go slowly from the green dot to the star without lifting the pencil.
home: Draw lines in a tray of flour or sand.
Pick up chickpeas one at a time to build finger strength.
guide.watch: A fist grip is common at this age. Gently move the fingers into a pinch and keep sessions short.

Ask "how many?" and let your child say the last number.
Show the number card that matches the group.
home: Count spoons, shoes or biscuits at home.
Hold up fingers quickly and ask how many.
guide.watch: Children often count an object twice or skip one. Move each object aside as you count it.

steps: Play "touch your nose, touch your ears".
Talk about what each sense does: eyes see, ears hear.
Make hand washing a song: count to 20 while washing.
home: Sing a body parts song with actions.
Play a smell or taste guessing game with safe foods.
guide.watch: Mixing up left and right is fine at this age. Just name the body part.

Trace each line in the air from right to left.
Trace on paper from the green dot to the star.
home: Draw right-to-left lines in a tray of flour.
Practise with a finger on a takhti or chalkboard.

Say a short word slowly and ask which vowel is in the middle.
Change the vowel to make new words: cat, cot, cut.

Play vowel I Spy.
guide.watch: Short e and short i sound close. Exaggerate them: "e-e-egg", "i-i-itch".

Talk about what we wear and eat in each season.
Keep a simple weather chart for a week.
home: Draw a sun, cloud or raindrop on the calendar each day.
Sort winter and summer clothes together.
guide.watch: Seasons feel abstract. Link each one to something your child remembers, like mangoes in summer.

Test objects against the list.

home: Go on a living and non-living hunt in the garden.
Watch a plant grow over a week.
guide.watch: Children think anything that moves is alive (clouds, cars). Use the full list, not just movement.

Compare a stone tool with a knife at home.
Make a simple then-and-now chart.

Try grinding grain between two stones.
guide.watch: Early history covers a very long time. A simple timeline from long ago to now helps.

Draw the way from home to school.
guide.watch: Children mix up left and right with east and west. Directions stay the same when you turn around.

Make a two-column list: village, city.
guide.watch: Villages and cities need each other: food comes from villages, many goods come from cities.

Play "one or many" with toys.

Draw a picture of your favourite part of nature.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

Record your voice with the microphone.
home: Make an input and output poster.
Find input and output devices on a phone.

Plan a healthy plate together.
