Read a sentence and find one of each.
home: Play noun and verb charades.
Make silly sentences with one noun and one verb.
guide.watch: Some words can be both (a run, to run). Ask what the word is doing in that sentence.

title: Adjectives Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English practice on adjectives, from "Describing Words" to "Describe It". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Adjectives describe nouns: size, colour, feeling, taste and more.
steps: Hold an object and ask "what is it like?"
Collect the describing words on paper.
Use two adjectives in one sentence: a big, red ball.
home: Play "I am thinking of something soft and white".
Describe dinner with three adjectives.
guide.watch: Children use "nice" and "good" for everything. Make a list of better words together.

title: Sentences and punctuation Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English practice on sentences and punctuation, from "Capitals and Full Stops" to "Build a Sentence". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use capital letters and full stops.
Order words to make a sentence.

guide.what: A sentence starts with a capital letter, ends with a full stop or question mark, and makes sense.
steps: Show a sentence and point to the capital and the full stop.
Say a telling sentence and an asking sentence; hear the difference.
Mix up the words of a sentence and put them back in order.
home: Write a shopping list as full sentences.
Play "question or telling?" in the car.
guide.watch: Names of people and places need capitals too, like Ali and Lahore.

title: Pronouns, is/am/are and past tense Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English practice on pronouns, is/am/are and past tense, from "Am, Is, Are" to "And, But, Because". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use am, is and are with pronouns.
Write the simple past of regular verbs.
Join ideas with and, but and because.

guide.what: Using am, is and are correctly, writing the past with -ed, and joining ideas with and, but and because.
steps: Make a chart: I am, he is, they are.
Talk about yesterday and stress the -ed ending.
Finish sentences together: "I am tired because..."
home: At dinner, ask: What did you do today? Answer with -ed verbs.
Play "but" sentences: "I like rain, but..."
guide.watch: Children may say "goed" for went. It shows they know the rule. Say the correct form back gently.

title: Blends and long vowels Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English practice on blends and long vowels, from "Blends" to "Y at the End". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read and spell words with initial blends.
Read long vowel sounds spelt ai, ee and oa.

guide.what: Two consonants blended together, long vowel sounds made by vowel teams, and the two sounds of y.
steps: Say each sound in a blend quickly: s-t, st.
Teach "when two vowels go walking, the first one does the talking" for ai, ee and oa.
Sort word cards into piles by sound.
home: Find blends on shop signs: stop, sweets, fresh.
Read a page of a storybook and look for ee and oa words.
guide.watch: The rule about vowel teams is a helpful guide but has exceptions (bread). Treat exceptions as tricky words.

title: Poems about the world Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English practice on poems about the world, from "My Shadow" to "Write a Colour Poem". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read a poem with rhythm and expression.
Find colour words and rhymes in a poem.
Write a short guided poem using rhyming words.

guide.what: Reading classic poems aloud, finding rhymes and colour words, and writing a short poem.
steps: Read the poem aloud with expression, then let your child read a line.
Clap the rhythm of one line.
Make a list of the rhyming pairs.
home: Go outside and make shadows at different times of day.
Write a colour poem about things at home.
guide.watch: A poem does not need to rhyme perfectly. Praise good describing words and a strong beat.

title: Reading for meaning Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English practice on reading for meaning, from "Eid at Nani's House" to "What Happens Next?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Predict what happens next and give a reason.

guide.what: Understanding a passage, answering in full sentences, telling facts from opinions and making predictions.
steps: Read the questions first, then the passage.
Underline the part of the passage that has the answer.
Answer using words from the question: "Where does Nani live? Nani lives in..."
home: Read the newspaper headlines together and find one fact.
Pause a story and ask: What will happen next?
guide.watch: One-word answers are fine for Grade 1. In Grade 2, encourage full sentences that start with the question words.

words: Zara wore a new green kurta.

title: My day and speech bubbles Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English practice on my day and speech bubbles, from "Order Words" to "Speech Bubbles". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use sequence words to write in order.
Write a short recount of a daily routine.
Write what characters say in speech bubbles.

guide.what: Writing in order with first, then, next and finally, and writing what people say.
steps: Talk through the steps out loud before writing.
Point to the order word at the start of each sentence.
Read the speech bubble lines in a funny voice.
home: Write the steps for making a sandwich together.
Draw a short comic strip with two speech bubbles.
guide.watch: Each sentence should start with a capital. A comma after First, Then and Next is good practice.

title: Synonyms and compound words Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English practice on synonyms and compound words, from "Same Meaning" to "Better Words". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Synonyms are words that mean the same; compound words join two words into one.
steps: Play "say it another way" with everyday words.
Find compound words on packets and signs.
Swap boring words for better ones in a sentence.
home: Make a word wall of synonyms.
Draw pictures of funny compound words like "butterfly".
guide.watch: Not every synonym fits every sentence. Read the new sentence aloud to check.

title: Writing a letter Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English practice on writing a letter, from "Parts of a Letter" to "My Letter". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the parts of a friendly letter.

guide.what: Writing a friendly letter with a greeting, message and closing.
steps: Look at a real letter or card together.
Talk about what to include in the message.
Post a real letter if you can.
home: Write an Eid card to a relative.
Make a classroom postbox at home.
guide.watch: Letters start with "Dear" and end with "From" or "Love from". Keep it simple.

title: The Alphabet Practice
subject: English Warm-up
desc: 4 pages of Grade 1 English Warm-up practice on alphabet, from "Missing Letters" to "Vowel Hunt". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Write capital and small letters in alphabetical order.
Match capital letters to their small letters.
Hear and identify the beginning sound of a word.
Recognise the five vowels and use them in short words.

guide.what: Letter names and sounds, and capital and small letters in order.
steps: Teach the sound first: "b" as in ball, then the name.
Show the capital and small letter side by side and trace both.
Sing the alphabet slowly while pointing to each letter.
home: Go on a letter hunt on packets and signboards.
Make letters with playdough or in a tray of flour.
guide.watch: b and d, p and q get mixed up. For b, say "bat then ball": the line first, then the circle.

title: Vocabulary Practice
subject: English Warm-up
desc: 4 pages of Grade 1 English Warm-up practice on vocabulary, from "My Classroom" to "Read and Answer". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name common classroom objects and use them in sentences.
Match common words to their opposites.
Sort words into groups by meaning.
Read a short story and answer simple questions about it.

guide.what: Everyday words, opposites, and how words fit into groups.
steps: Show the real thing while saying the word.
Use the word in a short sentence: "Put the pencil on the desk."
Sort words into groups such as fruit, colours and animals.
home: Label things at home with paper tags.
Play opposites: you say "big", your child says "small".
guide.watch: Explaining in Urdu is fine. Say the English word again afterwards so it sticks.

title: -ing Verbs Practice
subject: English Warm-up
desc: 4 pages of Grade 1 English Warm-up practice on -ing verbs, from "Adding -ing" to "What Are They Doing?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Add the -ing ending to action words.
Choose the correct -ing form to complete a sentence.
Link -ing action words to everyday places.

guide.what: Action words ending in -ing tell us what someone is doing right now.
steps: Do an action and say it: "I am jumping."
Write the action word, then add -ing in a different colour.
Ask what others are doing and answer in a full sentence.
home: Play charades and guess the action.
Describe what family members are doing right now.
guide.watch: Some words double a letter, like run and running. At this age, praise the idea and correct gently.

title: A, an, plurals and pronouns Practice
subject: English Warm-up
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English Warm-up practice on a, an, plurals and pronouns, from "A or An?" to "He, She, It, They". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use a before consonant sounds and an before vowel sounds.
Use the pronouns he, she, it and they.

guide.what: Using a and an, making plurals with s, and swapping names for he, she, it and they.
steps: Say a and an aloud: "an apple" is easier to say than "a apple".
Count things and add s: one shoe, two shoes.
Point to people and say he, she or they.
home: Name things at the dinner table with a or an.
Talk about the family using he, she and they.
guide.watch: "An" goes with the vowel sound, so it is "an hour" but "a uniform". At this age, practise the simple ones.

title: Word families and digraphs Practice
subject: English Warm-up
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English Warm-up practice on word families and digraphs, from "Word Families" to "ck, ll, ss, ff". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read words in the -at, -en and -ig families.
Read words with the digraphs sh, ch and th.
Spell words ending in ck, ll, ss and ff.

guide.what: Words that share an ending belong to a family, and some sounds are written with two letters.
steps: Write -at and change the first letter: c-at, h-at, m-at.
Blend each sound to read the word.
Notice double letters at the end of short words.
home: Make word family houses on paper: -at house, -en house.
Find ck words around the house: clock, sock, rock.
guide.watch: Children may write "duk" for duck. Teach that after a short vowel, the k sound is spelt ck.

title: Rhyming poems Practice
subject: English Warm-up
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English Warm-up practice on rhyming poems, from "Rain" to "Rhyming Pairs". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read a poem aloud and answer questions about it.
Recite a rhyme and recall details.

guide.what: Reading short poems aloud, feeling their beat and finding words that rhyme.
steps: Read the poem to your child, then together.
Clap the beat as you read.
Ask which words sound the same at the end.
home: Learn one short poem each week and say it to the family.
Make up a new line for the poem.
guide.watch: Poems are for saying aloud. Expression matters more than perfect reading at this age.

title: Read and answer Practice
subject: English Warm-up
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English Warm-up practice on read and answer, from "Ali's Kite" to "First, Next, Last". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Answer questions about a story with one word.
Put the events of a story in order.

guide.what: Reading a short story and answering who, what, where and when questions with one word.
steps: Read the story aloud together twice.
Find the answer in the story and underline it.
Retell the story in three steps: first, next, last.
home: Ask one question about every bedtime story.
Let your child ask you a question too.
guide.watch: If the answer is wrong, ask "Can you show me where it says that?" so your child learns to check the text.

title: Sentences about me Practice
subject: English Warm-up
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 English Warm-up practice on sentences about me, from "Fix the Sentence" to "Picture Story". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Begin sentences with a capital and end them with a full stop.
Write simple sentences with personal information.
Write sentences in order to tell a story.

guide.what: Writing short sentences about yourself with a capital letter, finger spaces and a full stop.
steps: Say the sentence out loud before writing it.
Count the words on your fingers.
Check for the capital letter and full stop at the end.
home: Write a sentence about your day in a little diary.
Write a card for a grandparent.
guide.watch: Spelling every word perfectly is not the goal yet. Praise complete sentences and fix one mistake at a time.

title: Parts of speech Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 English practice on parts of speech, from "Noun, Verb or Adjective?" to "Adverbs". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort words into nouns, verbs and adjectives.
Use pronouns to avoid repeating nouns.
Find and use adverbs that tell how.

guide.what: The main word classes: nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs.
steps: Colour-code a sentence: nouns blue, verbs red, adjectives green.
Replace nouns with pronouns to avoid repeating names.
Ask "how?" to find the adverb.
home: Play word-class bingo with a story page.
Make silly sentences: adjective, noun, verb, adverb.
guide.watch: Many adverbs end in -ly, but not all (fast, well). Ask what the word tells us about the action.

title: Prefixes and suffixes Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 English practice on prefixes and suffixes, from "Prefixes un- and re-" to "Word Meanings". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use the prefixes un- and re-.
Work out word meanings from prefixes and suffixes.

guide.what: Adding a prefix to the start or a suffix to the end of a word changes its meaning.
steps: Write the base word, then add the prefix in another colour.
Say what the prefix or suffix means.
Build a word family from one base: help, helpful, helpless, helper.
home: Play un- opposites: tidy, untidy.
Spot -ful and -less words in a newspaper.
guide.watch: Spelling sometimes changes when adding suffixes (happy, happiness). Teach the simple ones first.

title: Paragraph writing Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 English practice on paragraph writing, from "Topic Sentences" to "Write a Paragraph". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Choose a topic sentence for a paragraph.
Make a key word outline from a paragraph.
Write a paragraph from a key word outline.

guide.what: A paragraph has one main idea: a topic sentence, supporting sentences and an ending.
steps: Read a short paragraph and find its main idea.
Pick 2 or 3 key words from each sentence to make an outline.
Retell the paragraph from the key words, then write it in your own words.
home: After a trip, write three key words, then a short paragraph about it.
Read a paragraph aloud and ask your child to give it a title.
guide.watch: Copying sentences is not writing. Cover the original and write only from the key words.

title: Nouns, plurals and tenses Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 English practice on nouns, plurals and tenses, from "Common or Proper?" to "Past, Present, Future". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Identify past, present and future tense.

guide.what: Common and proper nouns, plurals that break the rules, and verbs in the past, present and future.
steps: Proper nouns are names: ask "Is it a special name?"
Learn tricky plurals as pairs: mouse, mice.
Look for time words: yesterday, now, tomorrow.
home: Find proper nouns in a newspaper and circle the capitals.
Tell a story about yesterday, today and tomorrow.
guide.watch: Children often write "childs" or "mouses". Keep a tricky plurals list on the fridge.

title: Spelling patterns Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 English practice on spelling patterns, from "Magic E" to "Sounds of -ed". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read and spell words with a silent e (magic e).
Spell words with silent b and k.
Hear the three sounds of the -ed ending.

guide.what: Spelling patterns: magic e, silent letters and the three sounds of -ed.
steps: Say the word with and without the magic e: cap, cape.
Point out letters we write but do not say.
Say -ed words and listen: is it t, d or id?
home: Write a list of silent letter words found in books.
Play magic e: write a word and let your child add e.
guide.watch: Spelling grows with reading. Children who read daily see patterns many times.

title: Classic poems Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 English practice on classic poems, from "Who Has Seen the Wind?" to "Acrostic Poem". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read a poem and understand its meaning.
Find adjectives and imagery in a poem.

guide.what: Reading classic poems for meaning, noticing describing words, and writing an acrostic poem.
steps: Read the poem aloud twice, slowly.
Ask: What picture does this poem make in your mind?
Underline the describing words.
home: Learn one poem by heart and say it to the family.
Write an acrostic for your name.
guide.watch: Poetry is meant to be felt. Ask "How does this poem make you feel?" as well as "What does it mean?"

title: Main idea and inference Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 English practice on main idea and inference, from "The Markhor" to "Road Safety". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Find the main idea of a passage.
Infer feelings and reasons from clues in a text.

guide.what: Finding the main idea of a passage and using clues to work out what the writer does not say.
steps: Ask: What is this passage mostly about? Say it in one sentence.
For inference, ask: What clues tell us that?
Answer with a reason: "I think... because..."
home: Watch a short video without sound and guess how people feel.
After a story, ask: Why did the character do that?
guide.watch: Inference is a big step. Model it: "Ammi's eyes are red and she is yawning. I think she is tired."

words: it is the safe place to cross

title: Diary, invitation and instructions Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 English practice on diary, invitation and instructions, from "An Invitation" to "My Diary". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Write an invitation with all the details.
Order the steps in a set of instructions.
Write a personal recount as a diary entry.

guide.what: Different kinds of writing: an invitation, step-by-step instructions and a diary entry.
steps: Look at a real invitation card and find who, what, when and where.
Follow a recipe together and number the steps.
Talk about the day before writing the diary.
home: Make an invitation for a family dinner.
Keep a diary for one week, writing three sentences each night.
guide.watch: A diary uses I and the past tense. Remind your child to say how they felt, not only what they did.

title: Punctuation Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 English practice on punctuation, from "Commas in Lists" to "Apostrophes". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use speech marks for spoken words.
Use apostrophes for contractions and ownership.

guide.what: Commas, speech marks and apostrophes make writing clear.
steps: Read a sentence aloud and pause at the comma.
Look at speech marks in a storybook.
Explain that an apostrophe shows a missing letter or ownership.
home: Write a short comic and turn the speech bubbles into speech marks.
Hunt for apostrophes on shop signs.
guide.watch: Its and it's are often confused. It's always means "it is".

title: Story writing Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 English practice on story writing, from "Beginning, Middle, End" to "Write Your Story". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the parts of a story.
Write a story with a beginning, middle and end.

guide.what: Planning and writing a story with a beginning, middle and end.
steps: Retell a favourite story in three parts.
Plan characters, setting and a problem together.
Use time words: one day, suddenly, in the end.
home: Tell a story together, taking turns with each sentence.
Write a story for a younger sibling.
guide.watch: Good stories have a problem. Ask: What goes wrong, and how is it fixed?

title: English Revision Set
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 English revision, one from each topic this term, with an answer key for every page.
obj: Revise every topic from the term before a test.

guide.what: The main word classes: nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs.
steps: Colour-code a sentence: nouns blue, verbs red, adjectives green.
Replace nouns with pronouns to avoid repeating names.
Ask "how?" to find the adverb.
home: Play word-class bingo with a story page.
Make silly sentences: adjective, noun, verb, adverb.
guide.watch: Many adverbs end in -ly, but not all (fast, well). Ask what the word tells us about the action.

title: English Warm-up Revision Set
subject: English Warm-up
desc: Ten pages of Grade 1 English revision: capital and small letters, beginning sounds, vowels, classroom words, opposites and adding -ing to action words. It ends with a short story to read and answer.
obj: Write capital and small letters in order and match them
Hear beginning sounds and recognise the five vowels
Use classroom words, opposites and word groups
Add -ing to action words and use them in sentences
Read a short story and answer questions

guide.what: Letter names and sounds, and capital and small letters in order.
steps: Teach the sound first: "b" as in ball, then the name.
Show the capital and small letter side by side and trace both.
Sing the alphabet slowly while pointing to each letter.
home: Go on a letter hunt on packets and signboards.
Make letters with playdough or in a tray of flour.
guide.watch: b and d, p and q get mixed up. For b, say "bat then ball": the line first, then the circle.

title: حروف اور جوڑ توڑ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on letters, joining and breaking (حروف اور جوڑ توڑ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Say and write the Urdu alphabet in order.

guide.what: The Urdu alphabet from alif to bari yay, and joining letters into words and breaking words back into letters.
steps: Say the alphabet together, pointing to each letter.
Join letters aloud: b plus a plus t makes baat.
Break a word by saying each letter slowly.
home: Make letter cards and build words on the floor.
Ask your child to break the name of a family member into letters.
guide.watch: Letters change shape when they join. Show the full letter next to its joined shape.

title: دو حرفی الفاظ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on two letter words (دو حرفی الفاظ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Sort two letter words ending in wao and yay.

guide.what: Reading and writing two letter Urdu words, including words that end in wao and yay.
steps: Read each letter, then blend them together.
Point to the joined letters as you read.
Use each word in a short spoken sentence.
home: Find two letter words on signs and packets.
Write two letter words with chalk or a finger in sand.
guide.watch: Some letters, like alif, dal and wao, do not join to the next letter. Point this out.

title: تین اور چار حرفی الفاظ کی مشق
en: Three and four letter words practice
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on three and four letter words (تین اور چار حرفی الفاظ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Make three and four letter words.
Count the letters in a word.
Use three and four letter words in sentences.

guide.what: Reading and writing three and four letter words, and counting the letters in a word.
steps: Blend the letters one by one.
Clap once for each letter.
Read the word in a sentence.
home: Label things at home: میز، کرسی، دروازہ.
Count the letters in names of fruits.
guide.watch: The letter ھ (do chashmi hay) counts as a letter, as in گھر.

title: اعراب: زبر، زیر، پیش کی مشق
en: Vowel marks: zabar, zer, pesh practice
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on vowel marks: zabar, zer, pesh (اعراب: زبر، زیر، پیش), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Sort words by zabar, zer and pesh.
Name the vowel mark in a word.
Use ا، و and ی for long sounds.

guide.what: The short vowel marks zabar, zer and pesh, and the long sounds made by alif, wao and yay.
steps: Say the word with each mark and hear the change: bas, bis, bus.
Draw the mark above or below the letter with a finger.
Stretch long sounds: baaat, moooor.
home: Write a word and let your child add the vowel mark.
Read a few words from a storybook with marks.
guide.watch: Zabar and pesh go above the letter, zer goes below. Children often mix up zabar and zer.

title: مد، تشدید اور ہمزہ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on madd, shadd and hamza (مد، تشدید اور ہمزہ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read and write words with madd.

guide.what: Three special marks: madd on alif makes a long aa sound, shadd doubles a sound, and hamza joins two vowel sounds.
steps: Say aam and am to hear madd.
Clap twice for a letter with shadd: am-mi.
Find the small hamza sign in words like چائے.
home: Spot madd, shadd and hamza in a storybook.
Make word cards for امّی، ابّو، بلّی.
guide.watch: Children often forget the madd on آ. Remind them that آم needs it.

title: ی، ے اور و کی آوازیں کی مشق
en: Sounds of yay and wao practice
topic: ی، ے اور و کی آوازیں
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on sounds of yay and wao (ی، ے اور و کی آوازیں), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Tell choti yay and bari yay apart.
Write words with yay in the middle.
Hear the different sounds of wao.

pages.title: چھوٹی یے اور بڑی یے
pages.topic: ی، ے اور و کی آوازیں

pages.title: درمیان میں ی
pages.topic: ی، ے اور و کی آوازیں

pages.title: و کی آوازیں
pages.topic: ی، ے اور و کی آوازیں

guide.what: Choti yay and bari yay at the end of words, the middle shape of yay, and the three sounds of wao.
steps: Bari yay sits on the line and swings out: گائے.
In the middle of a word, yay is just two dots under a small tooth.
Say doodh, mor and aur and listen to the wao.
home: Sort fruit and vegetable names by their last letter.
Read words with wao and say which sound they make.
guide.watch: Wao has three sounds: oo as in دودھ، o as in مور and au as in اور. Practise them by listening, not by rules.

title: میں اور میرا گھر کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on me and my home (میں اور میرا گھر), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read a short passage about a child and his home.
Name the parts of a house.

guide.what: Reading a short passage about a child and his home, naming the parts of a house, and writing about yourself.
steps: Read the passage aloud, one sentence at a time.
Ask who, what and where questions.
Help your child say sentences about themselves before writing.
home: Walk around the house and name each room in Urdu.
Make a small poster: میرا گھر.
guide.watch: When answering, children should use full sentences ending with ۔

title: میرا اسکول اور اچھی باتیں کی مشق
en: My school and good habits practice
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on my school and good habits (میرا اسکول اور اچھی باتیں), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read a short passage and answer questions.
Tell good habits from bad ones.

guide.what: Reading about school, naming school things, and talking about good and bad habits.
steps: Read the passage together and find the answers in it.
Talk about what your child does at school each day.
Discuss why each habit is good or bad.
home: Make a good habits chart and add a star each day.
Name five things in your child's school bag in Urdu.
guide.watch: Ask your child to explain why a habit is good, not just to pick the answer.

title: کہانی: شیر آیا شیر آیا کی مشق
en: Story: the boy who cried lion practice
topicEn: Story: the boy who cried lion
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on story: the boy who cried lion (کہانی: شیر آیا شیر آیا), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read a story and decide true or false.
Find the lesson of a story.

guide.what: A story about a shepherd boy who lied and was not believed when the danger was real.
steps: Read the story aloud with expression.
Stop and ask: why did the villagers come?
Talk about why telling the truth matters.
home: Act out the story with toys.
Ask your child to retell it in their own words.
guide.watch: Make sure your child understands why nobody came at the end. That is the lesson.

title: سبزیاں، پھل اور بارش کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on vegetables, fruit and rain (سبزیاں، پھل اور بارش), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Match fruits and vegetables to their colours.
Read about a rainy day and answer.

guide.what: Names of vegetables and fruits, their colours, and a short passage about a rainy day.
steps: Name each fruit and vegetable aloud.
Say its colour in Urdu.
Read the rain passage and find the answers.
home: Name vegetables and fruits in Urdu at the market.
Make a paper boat together on a rainy day.
guide.watch: Some children call tomato a fruit. Here it is sorted as a vegetable, as we cook it like one.

زبر، زیر، پیش اور ا، و، ی کی آوازیں پہچاننا

guide.what: Most Urdu letters change shape when they join the next letter. These joining forms are the چھوٹی اشکال.
steps: Write the full letter and its short form side by side, like ب and بـ.
Join two or three letters slowly to make a word, saying each sound.
Break the word back into its letters.
home: Write family names and break them into letters.
Trace letters in a tray of flour or sand.
guide.watch: The dots travel with the short form. Check they are in the right place and the right number.

obj: Write the short (joining) form of Urdu letters.
Join letters using short forms to write whole words.

steps: Write the full letter and its short form side by side, like ب and بـ.
Join two or three letters slowly to make a word, saying each sound.
Break the word back into its letters.

Trace letters in a tray of flour or sand.
guide.watch: The dots travel with the short form. Check they are in the right place and the right number.

title: شرارتی نو کی مشق
subject: Urdu Warm-up
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on the naughty nine (شرارتی نو), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Recognise the nine letters that do not join to the next letter.
Write words that contain non-joining letters.

pages.title: لفظوں میں شرارتی حروف
pages.en: Find the naughty nine in words

guide.what: Nine letters never join to the letter after them: ا د ڈ ذ ر ڑ ز ژ و.
steps: Learn the nine as a group, like a rhyme.
Show a word like دروازہ where these letters stay apart.
Circle the naughty letters in short words.
home: Hunt for them in a newspaper headline.
Make nine cards and play a memory game.
guide.watch: Children often try to join these letters forward. Remind them the naughty nine never hold the next letter's hand.

title: مصوّتے کی مشق
subject: Urdu Warm-up
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on vowel sounds (مصوّتے), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Recognise the short vowel marks zabar, zer and pesh.
Sort words by the vowel mark on the first letter.
Blend letters with ا، و، ی to make long vowel sounds.

guide.what: Zabar, zer and pesh give short sounds; ا و ی give long sounds.
steps: Use hand signals: zabar hand up, zer hand down, pesh hand forward.
Read بَ بِ بُ, then با بی بو, and listen for the difference.
Read short words that have the marks on them.
home: Say two words for each mark.
Spot ا و ی on signboards.
guide.watch: Short and long sounds get mixed up. Stretch the long sounds when you read aloud.

title: بصری الفاظ کی مشق
subject: Urdu Warm-up
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on sight words (بصری الفاظ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read and use common sight words in sentences.
Choose the correct sight word to complete a sentence.
Use more sight words in sentences.

guide.what: Small common words like ہے، میں، اور، کی that children learn to read on sight.
steps: Make word cards and read five every day.
Find the words in a short story.
Make a sentence using one sight word.
home: Stick word cards on the fridge.
Read a story and count how many times ہے appears.
guide.watch: Short daily practice works better than one long session.

title: واحد اور جمع کی مشق
subject: Urdu Warm-up
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on one and many (واحد اور جمع), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Use singular and plural in sentences.

guide.what: Singular and plural words in Urdu.
steps: Count objects and say one or many in Urdu.
Show patterns: ا becomes ے, ی becomes یاں.
Play "ایک یا بہت" with toys.
home: Count fruit at the market in Urdu.
Make word cards for singular and plural pairs.
guide.watch: Some words stay the same (درخت، پھول). Learn them as special words.

title: نظم: بچے کی دعا کی مشق
subject: Urdu Warm-up
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on poem: a child's prayer (نظم: بچے کی دعا), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read and recite a famous Urdu poem.
Learn meanings of words in the poem.

guide.what: Reading and reciting Allama Iqbal's poem "Bachay ki Dua" and learning its words.
steps: Recite the poem together each morning.
Explain each hard word with an example.
Talk about how a candle gives light to others.
home: Learn the first two couplets by heart.
Light a candle and talk about the meaning.
guide.watch: Many schools recite this poem in assembly. Knowing it well builds confidence.

title: کہانی پڑھیں کی مشق
subject: Urdu Warm-up
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on reading a story (کہانی پڑھیں), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Answer questions about a story in one word.
Order the events of a story.

guide.what: Reading a short Urdu story and answering questions about it.
steps: Read the story aloud together.
Ask: کیا، کون، کہاں؟
Retell the story in three steps.
home: Read an Urdu story book at bedtime.
Act out the story with stones and a glass of water.
guide.watch: This is a story of thinking hard. Ask your child what they would have done.

title: جملے بنائیں کی مشق
subject: Urdu Warm-up
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on making sentences (جملے بنائیں), with an answer key for every page.

guide.what: Making short sentences in Urdu.
steps: Say a sentence aloud before writing it.
Point to each word as you read.
Check the sentence ends with ۔
home: Write a short Urdu sentence about your day.
Make sentences with word cards.
guide.watch: Word order in Urdu puts the verb at the end. Read sentences aloud to hear it.

title: Kinds of nouns Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on kinds of nouns, from "Common, Proper or Collective?" to "Abstract Nouns". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort common, proper and collective nouns.

guide.what: Nouns come in kinds: common, proper, collective and abstract (things we feel or think but cannot touch).
steps: Ask: is it any thing (common) or a special name (proper)?
Groups have their own names: a herd, a flock, a team.
If you cannot touch, see or hear it, it may be an abstract noun: love, fear, honesty.
home: Spot collective nouns at the zoo or market: a bunch of bananas, a crowd of people.
Name a feeling for each family member: Dada's patience, Ammi's kindness.
guide.watch: Abstract nouns are the hardest. Link them to feelings and ideas the child already knows.

title: Tenses Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on tenses, from "Simple Past" to "Which Tense?". An answer key for every page is at the back.

guide.what: Tenses tell us when something happens: simple present, present continuous, simple past and simple future.
steps: Look for time clues: every day, now, yesterday, tomorrow.
Learn irregular past verbs in pairs: go, went; see, saw.
For things happening now, use am, is or are with an -ing verb.
home: At dinner, each person says one thing they did, are doing and will do.
Make a fridge list of tricky past verbs and add one each day.
guide.watch: Children often write "goed" or "writed". Praise the try, then say the correct word.

title: Subject and verb agreement Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on subject and verb agreement, from "Is, Are, Was, Were" to "Adding -s or -es". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use is, are, was and were correctly.
Make verbs agree with singular and plural subjects.
Add -s or -es to verbs with he, she and it.

pages.title: Has or Have, Do or Does

guide.what: The verb must match its subject: one person or thing takes is, has, does or an -s verb; many take are, have, do.
steps: Find the subject first: who or what is doing the action?
One subject: is, was, has, does, runs. Many: are, were, have, do, run.
Words ending in s, sh, ch, x or o add -es: watches, fixes, goes.
home: Read sentences aloud and let your child spot the mismatch: "The boys is playing."
Make two columns on paper: one person and many people. Add sentences to each.
guide.watch: "I" and "you" take have and are, not has and is. This often confuses children.

title: Comparing adjectives Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on comparing adjectives, from "-er and -est" to "Good, Better, Best". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use more and most with long adjectives.

guide.what: Adjectives can compare: tall, taller, tallest. Long adjectives use more and most. Some words change completely: good, better, best.
steps: Use -er to compare two things and -est for three or more.
Short words double the last letter after a short vowel: big, bigger.
Long words take more and most: more careful, most beautiful.
home: Compare family members: who is tallest, oldest, fastest?
Line up three fruits and describe them: big, bigger, biggest.
guide.watch: Never use both: "more taller" is wrong. Choose -er or more, not both.

title: Prepositions and conjunctions Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on prepositions and conjunctions, from "Prepositions" to "Join the Sentences". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use prepositions of place and time.
Choose conjunctions: and, but, because, so.

guide.what: Prepositions show where or when (in, on, at, under). Conjunctions join ideas (and, but, because, so).
steps: Use at for clock times, on for days and in for months and years.
And adds, but shows a difference, because gives a reason, so gives a result.
Read the joined sentence aloud to check it makes sense.
home: Hide a toy and give clues: it is under, between or behind something.
Start a sentence and let your child finish it with because or so.
guide.watch: Children overuse "and then". Show how because and so make writing clearer.

title: Apostrophes and commas Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on apostrophes and commas, from "Short Forms" to "Commas in Lists". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use commas to separate items in a list.

guide.what: An apostrophe shows missing letters (don't) or belonging (Ali's bag). Commas separate things in a list.
steps: In short forms, the apostrophe goes where the letters are missing.
For belonging, add 's to the owner: the teacher's pen.
In a list, put commas between items and use and before the last one.
home: Find short forms in a storybook and say the long form.
Label things at home: Ammi's chair, Abbu's phone.
guide.watch: Its (belonging) and it's (it is) are different. Only it's has an apostrophe.

title: Direct speech Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on direct speech, from "Speech Marks" to "Who Is Speaking?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Choose speech verbs that show how words are said.

guide.what: Direct speech shows the exact words someone says, inside speech marks, with a capital letter and punctuation inside the marks.
steps: Put speech marks around the spoken words only.
Start the spoken words with a capital letter.
Put the comma, question mark or full stop inside the closing speech marks.
home: Read a comic together and turn one speech bubble into a sentence with speech marks.
Act out a short talk, then write it down.
guide.watch: Children often put the full stop outside the speech marks. Check this first.

title: Synonyms, antonyms and homophones Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on synonyms, antonyms and homophones, from "Homophones" to "Antonyms". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Choose between words that sound the same.

guide.what: Synonyms mean the same, antonyms mean the opposite, and homophones sound the same but are spelled differently.
steps: Use the sentence to decide which homophone fits.
Try a synonym in the sentence: does it still make sense?
Learn antonyms in pairs: arrive, depart.
home: Play the opposite game on a car ride: say a word, your child says its opposite.
Swap one word in a story with a better synonym.
guide.watch: There, their and they're are the trickiest. Teach one at a time.

title: Reading: sequencing and summarising Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on reading: sequencing and summarising, from "How Mangoes Reach Us" to "Summarise It". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Find the order of steps in an information text.
Sequence the stages of a process.
Summarise a short story in one sentence.

guide.what: Putting events and steps in order, and summarising a text in one or two sentences.
steps: Look for order words: first, next, then, finally.
Retell the text in order using your fingers: 1, 2, 3, 4.
For a summary, say who, what happened and how it ended in one sentence.
home: After a story, ask your child to retell it in three sentences.
Write the steps of a recipe in order together.
guide.watch: A summary is short. Children often retell every detail. Ask: what are the most important parts?

title: Letters and emails Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on letters and emails, from "Parts of a Letter" to "Write an Email". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the parts of a letter.
Tell formal and informal writing apart.

guide.what: Letters and emails have a greeting, a body and a closing. Formal ones are polite and serious; informal ones are friendly.
steps: Start with a greeting and end with a closing and your name.
Keep one idea in each short paragraph.
Choose formal words for a teacher or principal, friendly words for family.
home: Write a real letter to a grandparent and post it together.
Help your child write a short email to a cousin, with a clear subject line.
guide.watch: A subject line should say what the email is about in a few words, not "Hi".

Find nouns in a short Urdu story.
home: Play "name ten things in the kitchen".
Underline nouns in a newspaper headline.
guide.watch: Children sometimes pick adjectives (بڑا) as nouns. Ask: is it the name of something?

title: Maths Writing Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 4 pages of Nursery maths writing in a square-grid copy: write numbers, sums and tables neatly in boxes.

guide.what: Counting up to 5 objects, saying one number for each, and knowing the numerals 1 to 5.
steps: Line up five objects and touch each one as you count.
Ask "how many?" and let your child say the last number.
Show the number card that matches the group.
home: Count spoons, shoes or biscuits at home.
Hold up fingers quickly and ask how many.
guide.watch: Children often count an object twice or skip one. Move each object aside as you count it.

title: Maths Writing Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 6 pages of KG maths writing in a square-grid copy: write numbers, sums and tables neatly in boxes.

guide.what: Counting objects to 20 and reading and writing the numbers 11 to 20.
steps: Count real objects to 20, moving each one as you count.
Point out that 11 to 19 start with 1: one ten and some more.
Fill a number track together.
home: Count cars on the road up to 20.
Make a 1 to 20 number line on the floor with tape.
guide.watch: Teen numbers are tricky: we say "four" first in fourteen but write the 1 first.

title: Maths Writing Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 6 pages of Grade 1 maths writing in a square-grid copy: write numbers, sums and tables neatly in boxes.

guide.what: Your child counts objects to 20, reads and writes the numbers, and learns that 11 to 19 are one ten and some ones.
steps: Count real things, touching each one as you say the number.
Write 1 to 20 on a strip of paper. Point as you count forwards, then backwards.
Show 14 as a bundle of 10 sticks and 4 loose sticks: one ten and four ones.
home: Count rotis, stairs or cars on the road.
Ask: What comes after 13? What comes before 20?
guide.watch: Teen numbers are often written backwards, like 41 for 14. Say "ten comes first" and write the 1 first.

title: Maths Writing Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 6 pages of Grade 2 maths writing in a square-grid copy: write numbers, sums and tables neatly in boxes.
obj: Multiply two-digit numbers by one-digit numbers.

guide.what: Reading, writing and comparing numbers to 1000 using hundreds, tens and ones.
steps: Show 100 as ten bundles of 10 sticks.
Build a number like 345 with bundles and loose sticks.
Compare numbers by looking at the hundreds first.
home: Read prices in the bazaar and say how many hundreds.
Count in tens and hundreds while walking.
guide.watch: A zero in the middle (708) confuses children. Say "no tens" out loud.

title: Maths Writing Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 6 pages of Grade 3 maths writing in a square-grid copy: write numbers, sums and tables neatly in boxes.
obj: Multiply three-digit numbers by one-digit numbers.
Write division facts from the times tables.

guide.what: Multiplying and dividing with the 3 and 4 times tables, and how the two are linked.
steps: Show 3 × 4 as 3 rows of 4 objects.
Share the same objects into equal groups to show division.
Write the fact family: 3 × 4, 4 × 3, 12 ÷ 3, 12 ÷ 4.
home: Share fruit equally among the family.
Arrange cups or chairs in rows and count them.
guide.watch: Division can mean "how many in each group" or "how many groups". Act out both.

title: English Warm-up Writing Practice
subject: English Warm-up
desc: 8 pages of Grade 1 English handwriting on four lines, like a school copy: trace, then write letters, words and sentences.
obj: Spell and write the days of the week.
Copy short sentences with capitals and full stops.

guide.what: Letter names and sounds, and capital and small letters in order.
steps: Teach the sound first: "b" as in ball, then the name.
Show the capital and small letter side by side and trace both.
Sing the alphabet slowly while pointing to each letter.
home: Go on a letter hunt on packets and signboards.
Make letters with playdough or in a tray of flour.
guide.watch: b and d, p and q get mixed up. For b, say "bat then ball": the line first, then the circle.
